Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\ck-plan # Planning Create detailed technical implementation plans through research, codebase analysis, solution design, and comprehensive documentation. ## Prerequisites - **ClaudeKit CLI required:** This skill requires `ck` CLI for plan operations. Run `npm install -g claudekit` if not installed. ## CLI Integration This skill orchestrates planning, but ClaudeKit CLI now owns the plan file scaffolding and phase state mutations whenever `ck` is available. Use these commands instead of hand-editing CLI-managed plan structure: ```bash ck plan create \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill ck plan create \ --global \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check --start cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan uncheck ck plan status /absolute/path/to/plan.md ck config ui --port 3456 ``` Rules: - Use `ck plan create` to scaffold `plan.md` and `phase-*.md` when the CLI is available. - Default scope is project-local (`./plans/` under the current project). - Global scope is conditional: use `ck plan create --global ...` or fall back to global scope only when no project context exists. - Use `ck plan check` / `ck plan uncheck` for phase status changes. - Do not hand-edit the phases table for status toggles or structural updates when CLI commands are available. - Use the dashboard at `http://localhost:3456/plans` for visual plan management. - **Overwriting phase stub files:** `ck plan create` scaffolds small boilerplate `phase-XX-*.md` stubs. Always **Read the stub before Write** — Claude Code enforces Read-before-Write on existing files; skipping the Read causes the Write to be rejected, wasting the Write's input tokens AND forcing a retry. The stubs are tiny (~15 lines), so the Read cost is trivial. Then Write the full content following the canonical template below. ### Canonical Phase File Template Use this structure when filling each `phase-XX-*.md`. Loaded once with the skill — no per-file Read needed to learn it. Frontmatter fields match the CLI's phase schema; section headers match `documentation-management.md` so phase files stay consistent across plans. ````markdown --- phase: title: "" status: pending # pending | in-progress | completed priority: P2 # P1 | P2 | P3 effort: "" # e.g. "4h", "2d" dependencies: [] # phase IDs this blocks on --- # Phase : ## Overview <1-2 sentences describing what this phase delivers> ## Requirements - Functional: ... - Non-functional: ... ## Architecture ## Related Code Files - Create: `path/...` - Modify: `path/...` - Delete: `path/...` ## Implementation Steps 1. ... 2. ... ## Success Criteria - [ ] ... ## Risk Assessment ```` **IMPORTANT:** Before you start, scan unfinished plans in the active scope first: - Project scope: `./plans/` - Global scope: the configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` If there are relevant plans overlapping your upcoming plan, update them as well. If you're unsure or need more clarifications, use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask the user. ### Scope Selection - **Project scope** is the default whenever the current working tree has project context. - **Global scope** is allowed only when: - the user explicitly asks for it via `--global`, or - there is no project context to anchor a local plan. - **No project context** means no `.git`, `package.json`, or `CLAUDE.md` was found in the ancestor chain. - Keep scope honest in prose and examples: the skill describes CLI-owned behavior, it does not implement scope resolution itself. ### Cross-Plan Dependency Detection During the pre-creation scan, detect and mark blocking relationships between plans: 1. **Scan** — Read `plan.md` frontmatter of each unfinished plan (status != `completed`/`cancelled`) 2. **Compare scope** — Check overlapping files, shared dependencies, same feature area 3. **Classify relationship:** - New plan needs output of existing plan → new plan `blockedBy: [existing-plan-dir]` - New plan changes something existing plan depends on → existing plan `blockedBy: [new-plan-dir]`, new plan `blocks: [existing-plan-dir]` - Cross-scope dependency → use `global:` or `project:` prefixes - Mutual dependency → both plans reference each other in `blockedBy`/`blocks` 4. **Bidirectional update** — When relationship detected, update BOTH `plan.md` files' frontmatter 5. **Ambiguous?** → Use `AskUserQuestion` with header "Plan Dependency", present detected overlap, ask user to confirm relationship type (blocks/blockedBy/none) **Frontmatter fields**: ```yaml blockedBy: [260301-1200-auth-system] # Same-scope dependency blockedBy: [global:260301-1200-auth-system] # Cross-scope dependency blocks: [project:260228-0900-user-dashboard] # Explicit project-scope dependency ``` **Status interaction:** `ck plan status` is the authoritative inspection surface. Same-scope bare refs stay in the current scope; prefixed refs resolve against the explicit project/global root. Missing refs should warn and show `not found`, not hard-fail the plan. ## Default (No Arguments) If invoked with a task description, proceed with planning workflow. If invoked WITHOUT arguments or with unclear intent, use `AskUserQuestion` to present available operations: | Operation | Description | |-----------|-------------| | `(default)` | Create implementation plan for a task | | `archive` | Write journal entry & archive plans | | `red-team` | Adversarial plan review | | `validate` | Critical questions interview | Present as options via `AskUserQuestion` with header "Planning Operation", question "What would you like to do?". ## Workflow Modes Default: auto-detect planning mode (analyze task complexity and pick mode). | Flag | Mode | Research | Red Team | Validation | Cook Flag | |------|------|----------|----------|------------|-----------| | `--auto` | Auto-detect | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode | | `--fast` | Fast | Skip | Skip | Skip | (none) | | `--hard` | Hard | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | (none) | | `--deep` | Deep | 2-3 researchers + per-phase scout | Yes | Yes | (none) | | `--parallel` | Parallel | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | `--parallel` | | `--two` | Two approaches | 2+ researchers | After selection | After selection | (none) | **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): | Flag | Effect | |------|--------| | `--tdd` | Add tests-first structure to each phase for regression-safe refactors | | `--no-tasks` | Skip task hydration | Load: `references/workflow-modes.md` for auto-detection logic, per-mode workflows, context reminders. ## When to Use - Planning new feature implementations - Architecting system designs - Evaluating technical approaches - Creating implementation roadmaps - Breaking down complex requirements ## Core Responsibilities & Rules Always honoring **YAGNI**, **KISS**, and **DRY** principles. **Be honest, be brutal, straight to the point, and be concise.** ### 0. Scope Challenge Load: `references/scope-challenge.md` **Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task (single file fix, <20 word description) ### 1. Research & Analysis Load: `references/research-phase.md` **Skip if:** Fast mode or provided with researcher reports ### 2. Codebase Understanding Load: `references/codebase-understanding.md` **Skip if:** Provided with scout reports ### 3. Solution Design Load: `references/solution-design.md` ### 4. Plan Creation & Organization Load: `references/plan-organization.md` ### 5. Task Breakdown & Output Standards Load: `references/output-standards.md` ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Pre-Creation Check] --> B[Cross-Plan Scan] B --> C[Scope Challenge] C --> D[Mode Detection] D -->|fast| E[Skip Research] D -->|hard/deep/parallel/two| F[Spawn Researchers] E --> G[Codebase Analysis] F --> G G --> H[Write Plan via Planner] H --> I{Red Team?} I -->|Yes| J[Red Team Review] I -->|No| K{Validate?} J --> K K -->|Yes| V[Verification Pass] K -->|No| M[Hydrate Tasks] V --> L[Validation Interview] L --> M M --> N[Present Boundary Reminder] N --> P[Post-Plan Handoff
AskUserQuestion: skip gates already auto-run] P --> O[Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. ## Workflow Process 1. **Pre-Creation Check** → Check Plan Context for active/suggested/none 1b. **Cross-Plan Scan** → Scan unfinished plans, detect `blockedBy`/`blocks` relationships, update both plans 1c. **Scope Challenge** → Run Step 0 scope questions, select mode (see `references/scope-challenge.md`) **Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task 2. **Mode Detection** → Auto-detect or use explicit flag (see `workflow-modes.md`) 3. **Research Phase** → Spawn researchers (skip in fast mode) 4. **Codebase Analysis** → Read docs, scout if needed 5. **Plan Documentation** → Write comprehensive plan via planner subagent 6. **Red Team Review** → Run `/ck:plan red-team {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes) 7. **Post-Plan Validation** → Run `/ck:plan validate {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes) 8. **Hydrate Tasks** → Create Claude Tasks from phases (default on, `--no-tasks` to skip) 9. **Boundary Reminder** → Present optional next-step commands with absolute path 10. **Journal** → Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ### Whole-Plan Consistency Gate This gate is mandatory after `/ck:plan validate` or `/ck:plan red-team` edits any plan file. Load: `references/verification-roles.md` → "Whole-Plan Consistency Sweep". Before recommending `/ck:cook`, re-read `plan.md` and every `phase-*.md` file. Search all plan files for stale terms, rejected assumptions, renamed APIs/files/fields, superseded decisions, and duplicate embedded drafts/contracts. Reconcile contradictions across the entire plan, not only the edited phase. If unresolved contradictions remain, report them and ask the user. Do not recommend cook until the whole-plan consistency sweep reports zero unresolved contradictions. ## Output Requirements **IMPORTANT:** Invoke "/ck:project-organization" skill to organize the outputs. - DO NOT implement code - only create plans - Respond with plan file path and summary - Ensure self-contained plans with necessary context - Include code snippets/pseudocode when clarifying - Fully respect the `./docs/development-rules.md` file ## Task Management Plan files = persistent. Tasks = session-scoped. Hydration bridges the gap. **Default:** Auto-hydrate tasks after plan files are written. Skip with `--no-tasks`. **3-Task Rule:** <3 phases → skip task creation. **Fallback:** Task tools (`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskGet`/`TaskList`) are CLI-only — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for tracking. Plan files remain the source of truth; hydration is an optimization, not a requirement. Load: `references/task-management.md` for hydration pattern, TaskCreate patterns, cook handoff protocol. ### Hydration Workflow 1. Write plan.md + phase files (persistent layer) 2. TaskCreate per phase with `addBlockedBy` chain (skip if Task tools unavailable) 3. TaskCreate for critical/high-risk steps within phases (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Metadata: phase, priority, effort, planDir, phaseFile 5. Cook picks up via TaskList (same session) or re-hydrates (new session) ## Active Plan State Check `## Plan Context` injected by hooks: - **"Plan: {path}"** → Active plan. Ask "Continue? [Y/n]" - **"Suggested: {path}"** → Branch hint only. Ask if activate or create new. - **"Plan: none"** → Create new using `Plan dir:` from `## Naming` After creating plan: `node .claude/scripts/set-active-plan.cjs {plan-dir}` Reports: Active plans → plan-specific path. Suggested → default path. ### Important **DO NOT** create plans or reports in arbitrary user directories. **MUST** create plans or reports in one of these allowed roots: - project scope → current working project directory - global scope → configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` ## Subcommands | Subcommand | Reference | Purpose | |------------|-----------|---------| | `/ck:plan archive` | `references/archive-workflow.md` | Archive plans + write journal entries | | `/ck:plan red-team` | `references/red-team-workflow.md` | Adversarial plan review with hostile reviewers | | `/ck:plan validate` | `references/validate-workflow.md` | Validate plan with critical questions interview | ## Post-Plan Handoff (MANDATORY at session end) After `plan.md` + phase files are written and the user has reviewed/approved them, use `AskUserQuestion` to offer the appropriate next step. Recommend the option that best fits the plan's risk/scope; recommended option listed FIRST and labelled "(Recommended)". | Option | Recommend When | Why | |--------|----------------|-----| | `/ck:plan validate` | Plan is moderate-to-complex; user wants critical-questions interview before implementation | Cheapest gate — surfaces unspecified assumptions, missing acceptance criteria, hand-wavy phases | | `/ck:plan red-team` | Plan touches security, auth, payments, data integrity, public APIs, infra, or has high blast radius | Adversarial reviewers stress-test the plan for failure modes, attack vectors, and missing edge cases | | `/ck:cook ` | Plan is small / well-understood / low-risk and user wants to start implementation | Skip extra gates; go straight to implementation | | End session | User wants to review/share plan before deciding | Stop with plan path returned | **Skip this step ONLY when:** - The current invocation IS already a subcommand (`validate`, `red-team`, `archive`) — those have their own terminal handoff. - User explicitly said "just plan, don't suggest next step". **Skip an individual option ONLY when the active mode already auto-ran that gate (per Workflow Process Steps 6-7):** - Omit `/ck:plan red-team` from the offered options when mode is `--hard`, `--deep`, `--parallel`, or `--two` (Step 6 already ran adversarial review). - Omit `/ck:plan validate` from the offered options when mode is `--deep` (Step 7 already ran validation). - If both gates already ran, the Post-Plan Handoff still fires but offers only `/ck:cook ` and `End session`. After selection: invoke the chosen command with the plan path as argument for continuity. ## Quality Standards - Thorough and specific, consider long-term maintainability - Research thoroughly when uncertain - Address security and performance concerns - Detailed enough for junior developers - Validate against existing codebase patterns **Remember:** Plan quality determines implementation success. Be comprehensive and consider all solution aspects. ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:brainstorm` (after exploring options), `/ck:scout` (after codebase discovery) **May precede:** `/ck:cook` after user approval (otherwise stop with plan path and next-step options) **Related:** `/ck:brainstorm` (explore before planning), `/ck:cook` (execute after planning) ARGUMENTS: plans/260603-codeflow-ai-cost-intelligence-engine/brainstorm-final-260606.md

178	### 3.3 The Four Pillars

180	#### Pillar 1: PROVENANCE ENGINE — "WHO wrote this code?"
181	
182	**What it does:** Every code change touching AI tools gets a signed provenance record — ground truth capture at point of generation.
183	
184	**Technical mechanism:**
185	- PreToolUse hook captures: model_id, session context, human prompt intent
186	- PostToolUse hook captures: generated code hash (blake3), file paths, content diff
187	- Signed envelope: `{human_prompt_hash, model_id, model_version, code_hash, timestamp, developer_id}` → Ed25519 signature
188	- Compatible with [Agent Trace v0.1.0 spec](https://github.com/cursor/agent-trace) — JSON trace records, vendor-neutral
189	- Export as [SLSA provenance attestation](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/attestation-model) Level 2+
190	- Export as [CycloneDX AI-BOM](https://ebuildersecurity.com/cyber-news/g7-ai-sbom-framework-supply-chain-transparency-2026/) component
191	
192	**`codeflow blame` command:** Line-by-line attribution showing human vs AI, which model, which session, confidence level. Like `git blame` but for AI authorship.
193	
194	**Why ground truth > detection:**
195	- Exceeds AI: 95% accuracy via ML pattern matching → 5% error = liability in audit
196	- CODEFLOW: 100% accuracy via capture at point of generation → zero inference needed
197	- Regulatory requirement: [EU AI Act](https://www.wsgr.com/en/insights/2026-year-in-preview-ai-regulatory-developments-for-companies-to-watch-out-for.html) requires "transparency" — detection is opinion, attestation is evidence
198	
199	**Existing asset:** `session.rs` already captures PreToolUse/PostToolUse with blake3 hashing, file paths, tool names, content hashes. Gap: no signed envelope, no model ID extraction, no Agent Trace format export.
200	
201	#### Pillar 2: FINANCIAL CONTROL PLANE — "WHAT did it cost?"
202	
203	**What it does:** Attributes every token to a specific session → PR → feature → business outcome. Enforces budget policies.
204	
205	**Technical mechanism:**
206	- Token counting per tool call (already exists in `tracking.rs`)
207	- Session→PR linkage: extract PR number from git branch/commit metadata
208	- Cost calculation: model_id × token_count × current pricing → dollar cost per action
209	- Budget policies: per-developer caps, per-project caps, per-team caps
210	- Alert system: "Team X at 73% of monthly budget after 2 weeks"
211	- Automatic model routing: when budget tight → suggest cheaper model for simple tasks
212	- Cost-per-PR dashboard: "This PR cost $47 in AI tokens — 3x team average"
213	
214	**Why on-machine > billing API:**
215	- Vantage reads Anthropic/OpenAI billing API → knows total per user, NOT per PR
216	- CODEFLOW hooks see every tool call → knows exact tokens per file change per session
217	- Result: CODEFLOW can say "PR #1234 cost $47 across 12 Claude Opus sessions" — Vantage can only say "Developer X spent $430 this month"
218	
219	**Existing asset:** `tracking.rs` tracks input_tokens, output_tokens, tokens_saved per session. `events.proto` has CompressionEvent with token fields. Gap: no cost attribution to PR/feature, no budget policy engine, no model pricing lookup.
220	
221	#### Pillar 3: QUALITY GATE — "IS this code safe?"
222	
223	**What it does:** Pre-commit security and quality enforcement for AI-generated code.
224	
225	**Technical mechanism:**
226	- Hallucinated dependency detection: AI suggests `import foo_bar_baz` → check npm/PyPI/crates.io if package exists
227	- Vulnerability scanning: AI code through SAST patterns (already have security.rs with regex-based scanning)
228	- License compliance: check if generated code matches known copyleft-licensed code patterns
229	- Quality scoring: complexity metrics, test coverage requirements for AI-generated code
230	- CI/CD integration: `codeflow gate` command as pre-merge check — blocks PR if quality threshold not met
231	
232	**Why 27% hallucination rate matters:**
233	- [Sonatype 2026 report](https://www.sonatype.com/blog/what-the-2026-state-of-the-software-supply-chain-report-reveals-about-regulation): 27% of AI dependency suggestions are invalid or risky
234	- This isn't a nice-to-have — it's a production safety requirement
235	- Existing tools (Snyk, Checkmarx) scan ALL code — CODEFLOW scans AI-SPECIFIC code with AI-aware heuristics
236	
237	**Existing asset:** `security.rs` handles regex-based secret scanning. `waste.rs` detects wasteful patterns. Gap: no dependency validation, no license compliance, no CI/CD gate command.
238	
239	#### Pillar 4: COMPLIANCE ENGINE — "CAN you prove it?"
240	
241	**What it does:** Generates audit-ready compliance packages for EU AI Act, SOC 2, California AB 316.
242	
243	**Technical mechanism:**

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS: Final Brainstorm Report

**Date:** 2026-06-06
**Session:** Brainstorm #3 (final)
**Status:** READY FOR PLAN
**Previous reports:** brainstorm-report.md (session 1), brainstorm-review-260606.md (session 2)

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

CODEFLOW pivots from "token compression CLI" to **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** — the infrastructure layer that makes AI-generated code production-ready by answering 4 questions no one else answers simultaneously: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Position:** On-machine between developer and AI model — the ONLY point where human intent, AI action, code output, cost, and context ALL converge.

**Revenue model:** Usage-based SaaS ($15-45/dev/month), parasitic on enterprise AI coding spend ($9.8-11B market 2026, 47% CAGR).

**Why now:** Uber budget blowout + Microsoft license cancellations + EU AI Act Aug 2026 deadline + 42% code is AI-generated with zero traceability.

---

## PART 1: THE PROBLEM (VERIFIED, SOURCED)

### 1.1 Enterprise AI Cost Crisis — Happening RIGHT NOW

| Signal | Source | Impact |
|--------|--------|--------|
| Uber burned entire 2026 AI budget in 4 months | [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/05/26/uber-coo-ai-spending-tokens-claude-code/) | $500-2,000/dev/month, 84% of 5,000 engineers active |
| Microsoft cancelling Claude Code licenses by June 30 | [SpaceDaily](https://spacedaily.com/n-microsoft-is-canceling-claude-code-licenses-across-its-experiences-devices-division-by-june-30-steering-thousands-of-engineers-toward-github-copilot-while-uber-burned-through-its-entire-2026-ai-bu/) | Steering to cheaper Copilot CLI |
| One company spent $500M in single month | [BeInCrypto](https://beincrypto.com/enterprise-ai-cost-crisis-microsoft-uber/) | No usage limits set |
| 85% orgs miss AI cost forecasts by >10% | [Vantage](https://www.vantage.sh/blog/agentic-coding-costs) | 25% off by >50% |
| AI coding tools: $200-500/dev/month all-in | [Palma.ai](https://palma.ai/blog/real-cost-of-ai-coding-tools) | For 1,000 devs = $2.4-6M/year |
| Only 41% agent rollouts reach positive ROI in 12 months | [Gartner](https://www.gartner.com/en/articles/enterprise-ai-coding-agent-market) | 19% NEVER reach payback |

**Root cause:** AI pricing (per-token, per-API-call) doesn't map to per-seat/per-device models finance teams built forecasting around. "Meter runs when nobody is looking." [K]

### 1.2 Compliance Tsunami — Deadlines ARE SET

| Regulation | Deadline | What It Requires |
|-----------|----------|-----------------|
| EU AI Act (high-risk systems) | **Aug 2, 2026** | Transparency + audit trail for AI systems |
| EU Product Liability Directive | **Dec 9, 2026** | AI-generated code = product, **strict liability** |
| California AB 316 | **Jan 1, 2026** (active) | Eliminates "AI did it" defense — entire supply chain liable |
| EU Cyber Resilience Act | **Sep 11, 2026** | Vulnerability reporting for products with digital elements |
| G7 AI-SBOM Framework | **2026** | Model, dataset, component traceability required |
| SOC 2 CC6.1/CC8.1 | **Active** | AI code audit trails required for certification |

Sources: [Gibson Dunn](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-product-liability-directive-responding-to-software-ai-and-complex-supply-chains/), [Wilson Sonsini](https://www.wsgr.com/en/insights/2026-year-in-preview-ai-regulatory-developments-for-companies-to-watch-out-for.html), [BuildMVPFast](https://www.buildmvpfast.com/blog/ai-generated-code-liability-legal-risk-copyright-2026), [G7 AI-SBOM](https://ebuildersecurity.com/cyber-news/g7-ai-sbom-framework-supply-chain-transparency-2026/)

**Critical fact:** 42% of production code is now AI-generated, but most orgs cannot identify WHICH LINES. [K] A Fortune 500 fintech discovered 34% of their codebase was AI-generated during pre-IPO audit — they didn't know. [K]

### 1.3 Quality Crisis — Production Failures Rising

| Stat | Source |
|------|--------|
| 81% enterprise leaders report production issues increasing from AI code | [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/ai-ml/2026/05/20/ai-code-boom-drives-production-failures-higher-spending/5243787) |
| 27% of AI dependency suggestions are invalid or risky hallucinations | [Sonatype](https://www.sonatype.com/blog/what-the-2026-state-of-the-software-supply-chain-report-reveals-about-regulation) |
| 61% of average enterprise codebase now AI-generated or AI-assisted | [CloudBees](https://www.cloudbees.com/blog/2026-state-of-code-abundance-report) |
| AI productivity paradox: devs feel 20% faster but are 19% slower | [Exceeds AI](https://blog.exceeds.ai/industry-benchmarks-ai-code-productivity/) |
| Only 21% companies have mature AI agent governance | [Domino.ai](https://domino.ai/blog/the-autonomous-ai-agent-era-is-here-are-you-ready) |

### 1.4 The Four Questions Every Enterprise MUST Answer

Every line of code entering production needs answers to:

1. **WHO wrote it?** Human or AI? Which model? Which prompt? Who authorized?

### 3.3 The Four Pillars

#### Pillar 1: PROVENANCE ENGINE — "WHO wrote this code?"

**What it does:** Every code change touching AI tools gets a signed provenance record — ground truth capture at point of generation.

**Technical mechanism:**
- PreToolUse hook captures: model_id, session context, human prompt intent
- PostToolUse hook captures: generated code hash (blake3), file paths, content diff
- Signed envelope: `{human_prompt_hash, model_id, model_version, code_hash, timestamp, developer_id}` → Ed25519 signature
- Compatible with [Agent Trace v0.1.0 spec](https://github.com/cursor/agent-trace) — JSON trace records, vendor-neutral
- Export as [SLSA provenance attestation](https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.0/attestation-model) Level 2+
- Export as [CycloneDX AI-BOM](https://ebuildersecurity.com/cyber-news/g7-ai-sbom-framework-supply-chain-transparency-2026/) component

**`codeflow blame` command:** Line-by-line attribution showing human vs AI, which model, which session, confidence level. Like `git blame` but for AI authorship.

**Why ground truth > detection:**
- Exceeds AI: 95% accuracy via ML pattern matching → 5% error = liability in audit
- CODEFLOW: 100% accuracy via capture at point of generation → zero inference needed
- Regulatory requirement: [EU AI Act](https://www.wsgr.com/en/insights/2026-year-in-preview-ai-regulatory-developments-for-companies-to-watch-out-for.html) requires "transparency" — detection is opinion, attestation is evidence

**Existing asset:** `session.rs` already captures PreToolUse/PostToolUse with blake3 hashing, file paths, tool names, content hashes. Gap: no signed envelope, no model ID extraction, no Agent Trace format export.

#### Pillar 2: FINANCIAL CONTROL PLANE — "WHAT did it cost?"

**What it does:** Attributes every token to a specific session → PR → feature → business outcome. Enforces budget policies.

**Technical mechanism:**
- Token counting per tool call (already exists in `tracking.rs`)
- Session→PR linkage: extract PR number from git branch/commit metadata
- Cost calculation: model_id × token_count × current pricing → dollar cost per action
- Budget policies: per-developer caps, per-project caps, per-team caps
- Alert system: "Team X at 73% of monthly budget after 2 weeks"
- Automatic model routing: when budget tight → suggest cheaper model for simple tasks
- Cost-per-PR dashboard: "This PR cost $47 in AI tokens — 3x team average"

**Why on-machine > billing API:**
- Vantage reads Anthropic/OpenAI billing API → knows total per user, NOT per PR
- CODEFLOW hooks see every tool call → knows exact tokens per file change per session
- Result: CODEFLOW can say "PR #1234 cost $47 across 12 Claude Opus sessions" — Vantage can only say "Developer X spent $430 this month"

**Existing asset:** `tracking.rs` tracks input_tokens, output_tokens, tokens_saved per session. `events.proto` has CompressionEvent with token fields. Gap: no cost attribution to PR/feature, no budget policy engine, no model pricing lookup.

#### Pillar 3: QUALITY GATE — "IS this code safe?"

**What it does:** Pre-commit security and quality enforcement for AI-generated code.

**Technical mechanism:**
- Hallucinated dependency detection: AI suggests `import foo_bar_baz` → check npm/PyPI/crates.io if package exists
- Vulnerability scanning: AI code through SAST patterns (already have security.rs with regex-based scanning)
- License compliance: check if generated code matches known copyleft-licensed code patterns
- Quality scoring: complexity metrics, test coverage requirements for AI-generated code
- CI/CD integration: `codeflow gate` command as pre-merge check — blocks PR if quality threshold not met

**Why 27% hallucination rate matters:**
- [Sonatype 2026 report](https://www.sonatype.com/blog/what-the-2026-state-of-the-software-supply-chain-report-reveals-about-regulation): 27% of AI dependency suggestions are invalid or risky
- This isn't a nice-to-have — it's a production safety requirement
- Existing tools (Snyk, Checkmarx) scan ALL code — CODEFLOW scans AI-SPECIFIC code with AI-aware heuristics

**Existing asset:** `security.rs` handles regex-based secret scanning. `waste.rs` detects wasteful patterns. Gap: no dependency validation, no license compliance, no CI/CD gate command.

#### Pillar 4: COMPLIANCE ENGINE — "CAN you prove it?"

**What it does:** Generates audit-ready compliance packages for EU AI Act, SOC 2, California AB 316.

**Technical mechanism:**
- Aggregate provenance records into compliance reports
- Export formats: SLSA attestation bundles, CycloneDX AI-BOM, custom audit PDFs
- SOC 2 CC6.1/CC8.1 evidence packages: "here is every AI-generated code change, who authorized it, what model produced it, who reviewed it"
- EU AI Act transparency reports: AI system documentation per Article 11
- Retention policies: configurable data retention (default 90 days, enterprise 7 years)
- `codeflow audit` command: generate compliance report for date range

**Why compliance alone is NOT the product:**
Session 2 review correctly identified: compliance-only = boring, reactive, enterprise buys when fined. Compliance is a FEATURE of the supply chain OS, not the product itself. The product is: your AI code is production-ready. Compliance is one proof of that.

### 3.4 Proto Schema Extension Required

Current `events.proto` has 2 event types. Needed:

```protobuf
enum EventType {
  EVENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED = 0;
  EVENT_TYPE_COMPRESSION = 1;   // existing

  EVENT_TYPE_COST = 5;          // NEW: cost attribution

message ProvenanceEvent {
  string model_id = 1;
  string model_version = 2;
  string prompt_hash = 3;
  string code_hash = 4;
  string file_path = 5;
  uint32 start_line = 6;

  string attestation_sig = 9;

}

message CostEvent {

  string model_id = 2;

}

message GovernanceEvent {
  string policy_id = 1;
  string action = 2;            // allowed|blocked|downgraded
  string reason = 3;
  double budget_remaining_usd = 4;
  string developer_id = 5;
}

message QualityEvent {
  string check_type = 1;        // dependency|vulnerability|license|hallucination
  string severity = 2;          // critical|high|medium|low|info
  string file_path = 3;
  string finding = 4;
  bool blocked = 5;
}
```

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Codebase reality check:** RTK is 105 .rs files, ~69K LOC. Key assets to extend:
- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, token savings, daily/weekly/monthly stats
- `ccusage.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` — Claude Code spending data parsing + economics
- `hooks/` — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook system for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, etc.
- `discover/` — command classification + session analysis
- `filters/` — 65+ TOML-based output filters

**What does NOT exist yet:** protobuf schema, provenance records, signed attestation, budget policy engine, dependency validation, compliance exports, cloud backend (Go), ClickHouse, dashboard (Next.js).

**Target:** 12-week MVP across 7 phases. Phases 1-5 = CLI (Rust). Phase 6 = Cloud. Phase 7 = Launch.

## Brainstorm Source

`brainstorm-final-260606.md` — 3-session brainstorm, verified sources, competitive analysis of 12 competitors, 4-pillar architecture.

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort | Dependencies |
|-------|------|--------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | [Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core](./phase-01-foundation-proto-schema-provenance-core.md) | Pending | 2w | None |
| 2 | [Cost Attribution Engine](./phase-02-cost-attribution-engine.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 3 | [Budget Governance + Policy Engine](./phase-03-budget-governance-policy-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phase 2 |
| 4 | [Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection](./phase-04-quality-gate-dependency-hallucination-detection.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 5 | [Compliance Export Engine](./phase-05-compliance-export-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phases 1-4 |
| 6 | [Cloud Backend + Dashboard](./phase-06-cloud-backend-dashboard.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 5 |
| 7 | [OSS Polish + Launch Prep](./phase-07-oss-polish-launch-prep.md) | Pending | 1w | Phase 6 |

**Parallelism:** Phases 2-3 (cost) and Phase 4 (quality) can run in parallel after Phase 1.

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral (Rust CLI ↔ Go cloud)
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **SQLite (WAL mode) for local** — already proven in tracking.rs, extend for provenance/cost
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop
5. **blake3 for content hashing** — fastest cryptographic hash, already in Rust ecosystem

## Risk Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Hook API changes (Claude Code, Cursor) | Multi-agent support already in RTK; abstract hook interface |
| Protobuf adds build complexity | Use `prost` crate with build.rs; proto files in `proto/` dir |
| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine, optional org-managed keys later |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode + connection pooling (already used in tracking.rs) |

## Dependencies

- `prost` + `prost-build` — protobuf for Rust
- `ed25519-dalek` — Ed25519 signatures
- `blake3` — content hashing
- `ureq` — HTTP client (already in Cargo.toml)
- `serde_json` — JSON (already in Cargo.toml)

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Codebase reality check:** RTK is 105 .rs files, ~69K LOC. Key assets to extend:
- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, token savings, daily/weekly/monthly stats
- `ccusage.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` — Claude Code spending data parsing + economics
- `hooks/` — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook system for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, etc.
- `discover/` — command classification + session analysis
- `filters/` — 65+ TOML-based output filters

**What does NOT exist yet:** protobuf schema, provenance records, signed attestation, budget policy engine, dependency validation, compliance exports, cloud backend (Go), ClickHouse, dashboard (Next.js).

**Target:** 12-week MVP across 7 phases. Phases 1-5 = CLI (Rust). Phase 6 = Cloud. Phase 7 = Launch.

## Brainstorm Source

`brainstorm-final-260606.md` — 3-session brainstorm, verified sources, competitive analysis of 12 competitors, 4-pillar architecture.

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort | Dependencies |
|-------|------|--------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | [Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core](./phase-01-foundation-proto-schema-provenance-core.md) | Pending | 2w | None |
| 2 | [Cost Attribution Engine](./phase-02-cost-attribution-engine.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 3 | [Budget Governance + Policy Engine](./phase-03-budget-governance-policy-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phase 2 |
| 4 | [Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection](./phase-04-quality-gate-dependency-hallucination-detection.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 5 | [Compliance Export Engine](./phase-05-compliance-export-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phases 1-4 |
| 6 | [Cloud Backend + Dashboard](./phase-06-cloud-backend-dashboard.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 5 |
| 7 | [OSS Polish + Launch Prep](./phase-07-oss-polish-launch-prep.md) | Pending | 1w | Phase 6 |

**Parallelism:** Phases 2-3 (cost) and Phase 4 (quality) can run in parallel after Phase 1.

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral (Rust CLI ↔ Go cloud)
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **SQLite (WAL mode) for local** — already proven in tracking.rs, extend for provenance/cost
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop
5. **blake3 for content hashing** — fastest cryptographic hash, already in Rust ecosystem

## Risk Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Hook API changes (Claude Code, Cursor) | Multi-agent support already in RTK; abstract hook interface |
| Protobuf adds build complexity | Use `prost` crate with build.rs; proto files in `proto/` dir |
| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine, optional org-managed keys later |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode + connection pooling (already used in tracking.rs) |

## Dependencies

- `prost` + `prost-build` — protobuf for Rust
- `ed25519-dalek` — Ed25519 signatures
- `blake3` — content hashing
- `ureq` — HTTP client (already in Cargo.toml)
- `serde_json` — JSON (already in Cargo.toml)

# Phase 1: Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core

## Overview

Establish event schema (protobuf), content hashing (blake3), signed attestation (Ed25519), and the `codeflow blame` CLI command. This phase creates the data foundation all other pillars depend on.

## Requirements

- Functional: capture model_id, prompt hash, code hash, file paths, contributor type at point-of-generation via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; sign provenance records with Ed25519; export Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON; `codeflow blame` command shows line-by-line AI attribution
- Non-functional: <5ms hook latency (fail-open); provenance DB <50MB for 90 days typical usage; zero network dependency for local operation

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → extract model_id, prompt context
    ↓
PostToolUse hook → capture file diffs, compute blake3 hash
    ↓
ProvenanceRecord { model_id, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
    ↓
SQLite (provenance.db, WAL mode) ← stores locally
    ↓
Protobuf event → EVENT_TYPE_PROVENANCE → queued for cloud sync (Phase 6)
```

**Key decision:** Extend existing `hooks/hook_cmd.rs` PreToolUse/PostToolUse flow. Currently RTK hooks rewrite Bash commands. New hooks capture provenance metadata from the same JSON stdin without interfering with rewrite logic.

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add provenance capture to PreToolUse/PostToolUse handlers
- Modify: `src/hooks/mod.rs` — export new provenance module
- Modify: `src/core/mod.rs` — export provenance module
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `blame` subcommand
- Modify: `Cargo.toml` — add prost, prost-build, ed25519-dalek, blake3 deps
- Create: `proto/events.proto` — protobuf schema for all 7 event types
- Create: `build.rs` — prost-build compilation of proto files
- Create: `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord struct, signing, storage
- Create: `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management, sign/verify
- Create: `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 hashing for code content
- Create: `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export format
- Create: `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs` — `codeflow blame` command implementation

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add dependencies to Cargo.toml**
   - `prost = "0.13"`, `prost-types = "0.13"` (runtime)
   - `prost-build = "0.13"` (build-dependency)
   - `ed25519-dalek = { version = "2", features = ["rand_core"] }`
   - `blake3 = "1"`
   - `rand = "0.8"` (for key generation)

2. **Create `proto/events.proto`**
   - Define EventType enum (7 types per brainstorm §3.4)
   - Define ProvenanceEvent, CostEvent, GovernanceEvent, QualityEvent messages
   - Define EventEnvelope wrapper with timestamp, event_type, oneof payload

3. **Create `build.rs`**
   - Use prost-build to compile proto/events.proto → src/proto/mod.rs
   - Add to .gitignore: generated proto output (or check in — decide)

4. **Create `src/core/content_hash.rs`**
   - `fn hash_content(content: &[u8]) -> String` — blake3 hash, hex-encoded
   - `fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — hash file contents
   - `fn hash_diff(old: &str, new: &str) -> String` — hash the diff

5. **Create `src/core/attestation.rs`**
   - `struct KeyPair` — wraps Ed25519 keypair
   - `fn generate_keypair() -> KeyPair` — auto-generate, store at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
   - `fn load_or_generate() -> Result<KeyPair>` — lazy init
   - `fn sign(keypair: &KeyPair, data: &[u8]) -> String` — hex-encoded signature
   - `fn verify(pubkey: &[u8], data: &[u8], sig: &str) -> bool`

6. **Create `src/core/provenance.rs`**
   - `struct ProvenanceRecord` — model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, start_line, end_line, contributor_type (human|ai|mixed|unknown), attestation_sig, timestamp, developer_id, session_id
   - `struct ProvenanceStore` — SQLite-backed (new DB file `provenance.db` or extend `tracking.db`)
   - `fn record_provenance(...)` — insert record + sign with attestation
   - `fn query_by_file(path: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>` — for blame command
   - `fn query_by_session(session_id: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>`
   - Schema: `CREATE TABLE provenance_records (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT, ...)`

7. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - In PreToolUse handler: extract `model_id` from JSON context (Claude Code sends session info)
   - In PostToolUse handler: if tool was file-write/edit, compute blake3 hash of changed content
   - Create ProvenanceRecord, sign, store in provenance DB
   - Fail-open: if provenance capture fails, log warning but don't block the tool call

8. **Create `src/core/agent_trace.rs`**
   - Implement Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON format (per github.com/cursor/agent-trace spec)
   - `fn to_agent_trace(record: &ProvenanceRecord) -> Value` — convert to spec JSON
   - `fn export_agent_trace(records: Vec<ProvenanceRecord>) -> String` — full trace file

9. **Create `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow blame <file>` — line-by-line attribution
   - Output format: `<line_num> | <contributor> | <model_id> | <timestamp> | <code>`
   - Color-coded: human=green, ai=yellow, mixed=cyan, unknown=gray
   - Flag: `--json` for machine-readable output
   - Flag: `--session <id>` to filter by session

10. **Wire into main.rs**
    - Add `Blame` variant to Commands enum
    - Route to blame_cmd handler

11. **Tests**
    - Unit: content_hash (known vectors), attestation (sign/verify roundtrip), provenance (CRUD)
    - Integration: mock PreToolUse/PostToolUse JSON → verify provenance record created
    - CLI: `codeflow blame` on test fixture files

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `proto/events.proto` compiles with prost-build, generates Rust types
- [ ] Ed25519 keypair auto-generated on first use, persisted at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
- [ ] ProvenanceRecord created for every PostToolUse file-write event
- [ ] `codeflow blame <file>` shows line-by-line AI attribution with model_id
- [ ] Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export passes format validation
- [ ] Hook latency remains <5ms (benchmark test)
- [ ] Existing RTK tests still pass (no regression)
- [ ] 15+ new tests for provenance, attestation, content_hash, blame

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Claude Code doesn't expose model_id in hook JSON | HIGH | Parse from session metadata; fallback to "unknown" with flag |
| prost-build adds Windows build complexity | MEDIUM | Use pre-generated .rs files as fallback; CI builds on Linux |
| Provenance DB grows too large | LOW | 90-day retention (reuse tracking.rs pattern); vacuum on startup |

## Security Considerations

- Ed25519 private key stored with 0600 permissions (Unix) or ACL-restricted (Windows)
- Never log private key material
- Attestation signatures are non-repudiable — document this for users
- Content hashes use blake3 (cryptographic) not xxhash (fast but not cryptographic)

# Phase 2: Cost Attribution Engine

## Overview

Attribute every token to a specific session → PR → feature. Extend existing `tracking.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` with PR linkage, model pricing lookup, and cost-per-PR calculations. Add `codeflow cost` CLI command.

## Requirements

- Functional: link sessions to PRs via git branch metadata; calculate dollar cost per session/PR/feature; model pricing table (updatable); `codeflow cost` command shows cost breakdown by PR/dev/project
- Non-functional: cost calculation adds <1ms per event; pricing table updatable without recompile; backward-compatible with existing tracking.db

## Architecture

```
PostToolUse hook (existing) → token counts (already captured in tracking.rs)
    ↓
+ Extract PR ref from: git branch name, commit message, env vars (GH_PR_NUMBER)
+ Lookup model pricing: model_id → $/1K input tokens, $/1K output tokens
    ↓
CostRecord { session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db with cost_records table)
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_COST → queued for cloud sync
```

**Existing assets to extend:**
- `tracking.rs:TimedExecution` — already tracks input/output tokens per command
- `ccusage.rs` — already parses Claude Code spending from ccusage CLI
- `cc_economics.rs` — already computes cost-per-token, blended/active CPT
- `session_cmd.rs` — already analyzes sessions for RTK adoption

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add cost_records table, PR linkage fields
- Modify: `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs` — integrate per-PR cost rollups
- Modify: `src/analytics/session_cmd.rs` — add cost column to session analysis
- Modify: `src/analytics/mod.rs` — export cost module
- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — extract PR ref in PostToolUse, emit CostEvent
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `cost` subcommand
- Create: `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs` — `codeflow cost` command
- Create: `src/core/pricing.rs` — model pricing table + lookup
- Create: `src/core/pr_linker.rs` — git branch → PR linkage logic
- Create: `data/model-pricing.toml` — default pricing table (updatable)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `data/model-pricing.toml`**
   ```toml
   [models.claude-opus-4]
   input_per_mtok = 15.0
   output_per_mtok = 75.0
   cache_read_per_mtok = 1.5
   cache_write_per_mtok = 18.75

   [models.claude-sonnet-4]
   input_per_mtok = 3.0
   output_per_mtok = 15.0
   # ... etc for GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/pricing.rs`**
   - Load from `data/model-pricing.toml` (bundled) or `~/.config/rtk/model-pricing.toml` (user override)
   - `fn cost_for_tokens(model_id: &str, input: u64, output: u64, cache_read: u64, cache_write: u64) -> f64`
   - Fallback: if model_id unknown, use median pricing + log warning

3. **Create `src/core/pr_linker.rs`**
   - `fn detect_pr_ref() -> Option<String>` — try in order:
     1. Env var `GH_PR_NUMBER` or `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`
     2. Parse git branch name: `feat/PROJ-123-description` → `PROJ-123`
     3. Parse recent commit messages for `(#123)` pattern
     4. `gh pr view --json number` if gh CLI available
   - `fn detect_feature_tag() -> Option<String>` — from branch prefix or git tag

4. **Extend tracking.db schema**
   - New table: `cost_records (id, session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, project_path, developer_id, timestamp)`
   - Migration: add table if not exists (backward-compatible)

5. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - In PostToolUse: after existing token tracking, compute cost via pricing.rs
   - Detect PR ref via pr_linker.rs
   - Insert CostRecord into tracking.db
   - Emit EVENT_TYPE_COST protobuf event

6. **Create `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow cost` — summary of costs for current project
   - `codeflow cost --by pr` — cost breakdown by PR
   - `codeflow cost --by dev` — cost breakdown by developer
   - `codeflow cost --by model` — cost breakdown by model
   - `codeflow cost --by day` — daily cost trend
   - `codeflow cost --pr 1234` — specific PR cost detail
   - `codeflow cost --json` — machine-readable output
   - Reuse display_helpers.rs formatting patterns

7. **Extend `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs`**
   - Add `fn cost_per_pr(tracker: &Tracker, pr_ref: &str) -> PeriodEconomics`
   - Add PR column to economics table output

8. **Wire into main.rs**
   - Add `Cost` variant to Commands enum with subcommand args
   - Route to cost_cmd handler

9. **Tests**
   - Unit: pricing lookup (known model → expected cost), pr_linker (branch patterns)
   - Integration: mock PostToolUse → verify CostRecord in DB with correct cost_usd
   - CLI: `codeflow cost --by pr` with fixture data

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Model pricing table covers Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku), GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
- [ ] PR linkage detects PR ref from >=2 of the 4 detection methods
- [ ] `codeflow cost` shows total cost for current project with breakdown
- [ ] `codeflow cost --by pr` shows per-PR cost ranking
- [ ] Cost records stored in tracking.db, backward-compatible migration
- [ ] Existing `rtk economics` command still works (no regression)
- [ ] 12+ new tests for pricing, pr_linker, cost_cmd

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Model pricing changes frequently | LOW | TOML file updatable; CLI flag `--update-pricing` fetches latest |
| PR detection fails in detached HEAD CI | MEDIUM | Fallback to "unknown" PR; CI env vars as primary source |
| tracking.db migration breaks existing data | MEDIUM | ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN (SQLite supports); test migration path |

# Phase 3: Budget Governance + Policy Engine

## Overview

Real-time budget enforcement in PreToolUse hooks. Policy engine evaluates per-dev, per-project, per-team spending limits and can warn, downgrade model, or block tool calls that exceed budget.

## Requirements

- Functional: TOML-based policy definitions (per-dev, per-project, per-team limits); PreToolUse budget check (warn/downgrade/block); alert webhooks on threshold breach; `codeflow budget` CLI for status/policy management
- Non-functional: policy evaluation <2ms; fail-open if policy engine errors; policies hot-reloadable without restart

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → read accumulated cost for {dev, project, team} from tracking.db
    ↓
PolicyEngine.evaluate(context) → Verdict { Allow | Warn(msg) | Downgrade(to_model) | Block(reason) }
    ↓
If Block → return error JSON to agent (tool call rejected)
If Downgrade → rewrite model_id in hook response (redirect to cheaper model)
If Warn → log warning, allow tool call
    ↓
GovernanceEvent { policy_id, action, reason, budget_remaining, developer_id }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_GOVERNANCE → queued for cloud sync
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add budget check in PreToolUse before command rewrite
- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add query for accumulated cost by dev/project/team/period
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `budget` subcommand
- Create: `src/core/budget_policy.rs` — policy engine: load, evaluate, verdicts
- Create: `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs` — `codeflow budget` CLI
- Create: `data/budget-policy-example.toml` — example policy file

## Implementation Steps

1. **Define policy schema in `data/budget-policy-example.toml`**
   ```toml
   [global]
   period = "monthly"           # daily | weekly | monthly
   warn_at_pct = 75
   block_at_pct = 100

   [[limits]]
   scope = "developer"          # developer | project | team
   id = "*"                     # wildcard = all devs
   max_usd = 500.0
   action_on_exceed = "warn"    # warn | downgrade | block

   [[limits]]
   scope = "project"
   id = "frontend-app"
   max_usd = 2000.0
   action_on_exceed = "downgrade"
   downgrade_to = "claude-haiku-4"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "team"
   id = "platform"
   max_usd = 10000.0
   action_on_exceed = "block"
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/budget_policy.rs`**
   - `struct PolicyConfig` — deserialized from TOML
   - `struct PolicyEngine` — loads config, caches accumulated costs
   - `enum Verdict { Allow, Warn(String), Downgrade(String), Block(String) }`
   - `fn evaluate(&self, dev_id: &str, project: &str, team: &str) -> Verdict`
   - Load policy from: project `.codeflow/budget.toml` → user `~/.config/rtk/budget.toml` → bundled default
   - Accumulated cost query: sum cost_records WHERE dev/project/team AND period

3. **Extend PreToolUse in `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - Before command rewrite: run PolicyEngine.evaluate()
   - If Block: return JSON error `{"error": "budget_exceeded", "reason": "..."}`
   - If Downgrade: modify model_id in updatedInput/modifiedArgs
   - If Warn: write warning to stderr, continue

4. **Extend `src/core/tracking.rs`**
   - `fn accumulated_cost(&self, scope: Scope, id: &str, period: Period) -> f64`
   - Scope enum: Developer, Project, Team
   - Period enum: Daily, Weekly, Monthly (with start date calculation)

5. **Create `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow budget status` — current spend vs limits for all scopes
   - `codeflow budget set --scope dev --id alice --max 500` — quick policy update
   - `codeflow budget history` — spending trend with budget overlay
   - `codeflow budget alert --webhook <url>` — configure alert endpoint
   - Table output: scope | id | spent | limit | % | status

6. **Alert system**
   - On threshold breach: POST to webhook URL with JSON payload
   - Payload: `{ "event": "budget_warning", "scope": "developer", "id": "alice", "spent": 380, "limit": 500, "pct": 76 }`
   - Use `ureq` (already in deps) for HTTP POST
   - Async/fire-and-forget: don't block hook on webhook delivery

7. **Wire into main.rs**
   - Add `Budget` variant to Commands enum

8. **Tests**
   - Unit: policy parsing (valid/invalid TOML), verdict evaluation (under/warn/over)
   - Integration: mock PreToolUse with accumulated cost → verify block/downgrade/warn behavior
   - CLI: `codeflow budget status` with fixture policies

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Policy TOML parsed correctly with per-dev, per-project, per-team limits
- [ ] PreToolUse blocks tool call when budget exceeded (block action)
- [ ] PreToolUse downgrades model when budget tight (downgrade action)
- [ ] `codeflow budget status` shows current spend vs limits
- [ ] Webhook alerts fire on threshold breach
- [ ] Fail-open: policy engine error → tool call proceeds with warning
- [ ] 10+ new tests for policy engine, budget_cmd

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Blocking tool calls frustrates developers | HIGH | Default to warn-only; block requires explicit opt-in per policy |
| Model downgrade breaks agentic sessions | MEDIUM | Only downgrade for new sessions, not mid-session |
| Cost accumulation query slow with large DB | LOW | Index on (scope, period_start); same pattern as tracking.rs |

# Phase 4: Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection

## Overview

Pre-commit quality enforcement for AI-generated code. Detect hallucinated dependencies, vulnerable patterns, and license risks. `codeflow gate` command for CI/CD integration.

**Why Phase 4 can parallel Phases 2-3:** Quality gates depend on provenance data (Phase 1) to know which code is AI-generated, but don't depend on cost attribution (Phase 2) or budget governance (Phase 3).

## Requirements

- Functional: detect hallucinated npm/PyPI/crates.io packages; scan AI-generated code for vulnerability patterns; license compliance checks; `codeflow gate` as CI/CD pre-merge check; `codeflow scan` for ad-hoc scanning
- Non-functional: scan completes in <10s for typical PR (500 LOC changed); offline mode (cache registry data); exit code 0/1 for CI integration

## Architecture

```
codeflow gate (or pre-commit hook)
    ↓
1. Identify AI-generated files (from provenance DB, Phase 1)
    ↓
2. Extract dependencies: parse import/require/use statements
    ↓
3. Validate against registries:
   - npm: GET https://registry.npmjs.org/{pkg}
   - PyPI: GET https://pypi.org/pypi/{pkg}/json
   - crates.io: GET https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/{pkg}
    ↓
4. Scan code patterns (extend existing security.rs):
   - Known vulnerability patterns (regex-based, already exists)
   - Suspicious API usage (eval, exec, child_process)
   - Hardcoded secrets (already in security.rs)
    ↓
5. QualityEvent { check_type, severity, file_path, finding, blocked }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_QUALITY → stored locally + queued for cloud
    ↓
Exit code: 0 (pass) or 1 (blocked findings exist)
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/discover/rules.rs` — extend rule engine for quality checks
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `gate` and `scan` subcommands
- Create: `src/core/quality_gate.rs` — orchestrator: runs all checks, aggregates findings
- Create: `src/core/dep_validator.rs` — dependency existence validation against registries
- Create: `src/core/hallucination_detector.rs` — AI-specific hallucination patterns
- Create: `src/core/license_checker.rs` — license compliance scanning
- Create: `src/cmds/gate_cmd.rs` — `codeflow gate` CI/CD command
- Create: `src/cmds/scan_cmd.rs` — `codeflow scan` ad-hoc command
- Create: `data/quality-rules.toml` — configurable quality thresholds

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `src/core/dep_validator.rs`**
   - Parse import statements per language:
     - JS/TS: `import ... from 'pkg'`, `require('pkg')`
     - Python: `import pkg`, `from pkg import ...`
     - Rust: `use pkg::...` (check Cargo.toml deps)
     - Go: `import "pkg"` (check go.mod)
   - Registry validation with caching:
     - `fn validate_npm(pkg: &str) -> ValidationResult` — HEAD request to registry
     - `fn validate_pypi(pkg: &str) -> ValidationResult`
     - `fn validate_crates(pkg: &str) -> ValidationResult`
   - Cache results in SQLite (package_name → exists/not_found, checked_at)
   - Rate limiting: max 10 req/s to any single registry
   - Offline mode: use cache only, warn if cache miss

2. **Create `src/core/hallucination_detector.rs`**
   - Detect patterns known to be AI hallucination indicators:
     - Non-existent API methods on well-known libraries
     - Fabricated URL endpoints (check against known API patterns)
     - Import of packages with typosquat-like names (Levenshtein distance from real packages)
   - Severity levels: critical (definitely hallucinated), high (likely), medium (suspicious)

3. **Create `src/core/license_checker.rs`**
   - Extract license info from package registries (npm `license` field, PyPI classifiers)
   - Flag copyleft licenses (GPL, AGPL) in permissive-licensed projects
   - Configurable allowed/denied license lists in `quality-rules.toml`

4. **Create `src/core/quality_gate.rs`**
   - Orchestrator: runs dep_validator + hallucination_detector + license_checker + security.rs
   - Aggregates findings with severity
   - `fn run_gate(files: &[PathBuf], config: &QualityConfig) -> GateResult`
   - `struct GateResult { findings: Vec<Finding>, passed: bool, stats: GateStats }`
   - Blocking threshold configurable: block on critical+high, warn on medium+low

5. **Create `src/cmds/gate_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow gate` — scan staged files (git diff --staged)
   - `codeflow gate --all` — scan all AI-generated files in project
   - `codeflow gate --pr <ref>` — scan files changed in PR
   - `codeflow gate --json` — machine-readable output for CI
   - `codeflow gate --fix` — auto-fix where possible (e.g., correct package name)
   - Exit codes: 0 = pass, 1 = blocked findings, 2 = error

6. **Create `src/cmds/scan_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow scan <file>` — ad-hoc scan of specific file
   - `codeflow scan --deps` — dependency-only scan
   - `codeflow scan --security` — security-only scan
   - Reuse quality_gate.rs with subset of checks

7. **Create `data/quality-rules.toml`**
   ```toml
   [thresholds]
   block_on = ["critical", "high"]
   warn_on = ["medium", "low"]

   [licenses]
   denied = ["GPL-3.0", "AGPL-3.0"]
   allowed = ["MIT", "Apache-2.0", "BSD-2-Clause", "BSD-3-Clause", "ISC"]

   [registries]
   cache_ttl_hours = 24
   offline_mode = false
   ```

8. **Wire into main.rs**
   - Add `Gate` and `Scan` variants to Commands enum
   - Route to respective handlers

9. **Tests**
   - Unit: dep_validator with mock HTTP (known packages pass, hallucinated fail)
   - Unit: hallucination_detector with fixture code snippets
   - Unit: license_checker with known GPL/MIT packages
   - Integration: gate_cmd with staged files containing hallucinated deps → exit code 1
   - CLI: `codeflow gate --json` output validation

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Hallucinated npm/PyPI/crates.io packages detected with >95% accuracy
- [ ] Registry results cached in SQLite with configurable TTL
- [ ] `codeflow gate` blocks PRs with critical/high findings (exit code 1)
- [ ] `codeflow gate --json` outputs CI-compatible JSON
- [ ] License compliance flags copyleft in permissive projects
- [ ] Offline mode works with cached registry data
- [ ] 15+ new tests for dep_validator, hallucination_detector, gate_cmd

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Registry rate limits in CI (many PRs) | MEDIUM | Aggressive caching (24h TTL); batch requests; respect 429 |
| False positives on valid but rare packages | MEDIUM | Allowlist in quality-rules.toml; `codeflow gate --ignore <pkg>` |
| Import parsing misses edge cases | LOW | Start with common patterns; iteratively improve parser |

# Phase 2: Cost Attribution Engine

## Overview

Attribute every token to a specific session → PR → feature. Extend existing `tracking.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` with PR linkage, model pricing lookup, and cost-per-PR calculations. Add `codeflow cost` CLI command.

## Requirements

- Functional: link sessions to PRs via git branch metadata; calculate dollar cost per session/PR/feature; model pricing table (updatable); `codeflow cost` command shows cost breakdown by PR/dev/project
- Non-functional: cost calculation adds <1ms per event; pricing table updatable without recompile; backward-compatible with existing tracking.db

## Architecture

```
PostToolUse hook (existing) → token counts (already captured in tracking.rs)
    ↓
+ Extract PR ref from: git branch name, commit message, env vars (GH_PR_NUMBER)
+ Lookup model pricing: model_id → $/1M input tokens, $/1M output tokens
    ↓
CostRecord { session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db with cost_records table)
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_COST → queued for cloud sync
```

**Existing assets to extend:**
- `tracking.rs:TimedExecution` — already tracks input/output tokens per command
- `ccusage.rs` — already parses Claude Code spending from ccusage CLI
- `cc_economics.rs` — already computes cost-per-token, blended/active CPT
- `session_cmd.rs` — already analyzes sessions for RTK adoption

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add cost_records table, PR linkage fields
- Modify: `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs` — integrate per-PR cost rollups
- Modify: `src/analytics/session_cmd.rs` — add cost column to session analysis
- Modify: `src/analytics/mod.rs` — export cost module
- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — extract PR ref in PostToolUse, emit CostEvent
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `cost` subcommand
- Create: `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs` — `codeflow cost` command
- Create: `src/core/pricing.rs` — model pricing table + lookup
- Create: `src/core/pr_linker.rs` — git branch → PR linkage logic
- Create: `data/model-pricing.toml` — default pricing table (updatable)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `data/model-pricing.toml`**
   ```toml
   [models.claude-opus-4]
   input_per_mtok = 15.0
   output_per_mtok = 75.0
   cache_read_per_mtok = 1.5
   cache_write_per_mtok = 18.75

   [models.claude-sonnet-4]
   input_per_mtok = 3.0
   output_per_mtok = 15.0
   # ... etc for GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/pricing.rs`**
   - Load from `data/model-pricing.toml` (bundled) or `~/.config/rtk/model-pricing.toml` (user override)
   - `fn cost_for_tokens(model_id: &str, input: u64, output: u64, cache_read: u64, cache_write: u64) -> f64`
   - Fallback: if model_id unknown, use median pricing + log warning

3. **Create `src/core/pr_linker.rs`**
   - `fn detect_pr_ref() -> Option<String>` — try in order:
     1. Env var `GH_PR_NUMBER` or `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`
     2. Parse git branch name: `feat/PROJ-123-description` → `PROJ-123`
     3. Parse recent commit messages for `(#123)` pattern
     4. `gh pr view --json number` if gh CLI available
   - `fn detect_feature_tag() -> Option<String>` — from branch prefix or git tag

4. **Extend tracking.db schema**
   - New table: `cost_records (id, session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, project_path, developer_id, timestamp)`
   - Migration: add table if not exists (backward-compatible)

5. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - In PostToolUse: after existing token tracking, compute cost via pricing.rs
   - Detect PR ref via pr_linker.rs
   - Insert CostRecord into tracking.db
   - Emit EVENT_TYPE_COST protobuf event

6. **Create `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow cost` — summary of costs for current project
   - `codeflow cost --by pr` — cost breakdown by PR
   - `codeflow cost --by dev` — cost breakdown by developer
   - `codeflow cost --by model` — cost breakdown by model
   - `codeflow cost --by day` — daily cost trend
   - `codeflow cost --pr 1234` — specific PR cost detail
   - `codeflow cost --json` — machine-readable output
   - Reuse display_helpers.rs formatting patterns

7. **Extend `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs`**
   - Add `fn cost_per_pr(tracker: &Tracker, pr_ref: &str) -> PeriodEconomics`
   - Add PR column to economics table output

8. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Cost` variant to Commands enum

9. **Tests**
   - Unit: pricing lookup (known model → expected cost), pr_linker (branch patterns)
   - Integration: mock PostToolUse → verify CostRecord in DB with correct cost_usd
   - CLI: `codeflow cost --by pr` with fixture data
   - 12+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Model pricing table covers Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku), GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
- [ ] PR linkage detects PR ref from >=2 of the 4 detection methods
- [ ] `codeflow cost` shows total cost for current project with breakdown
- [ ] `codeflow cost --by pr` shows per-PR cost ranking
- [ ] Cost records stored in tracking.db, backward-compatible migration
- [ ] Existing `rtk economics` command still works (no regression)
- [ ] 12+ new tests for pricing, pr_linker, cost_cmd

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Model pricing changes frequently | LOW | TOML file updatable; CLI flag `--update-pricing` fetches latest |
| PR detection fails in detached HEAD CI | MEDIUM | Fallback to "unknown" PR; CI env vars as primary source |
| tracking.db migration breaks existing data | MEDIUM | ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN; test migration path |

# Phase 3: Budget Governance + Policy Engine

## Overview

Real-time budget enforcement in PreToolUse hooks. Policy engine evaluates per-dev, per-project, per-team spending limits and can warn, downgrade model, or block tool calls that exceed budget.

## Requirements

- Functional: TOML-based policy definitions (per-dev, per-project, per-team limits); PreToolUse budget check (warn/downgrade/block); alert webhooks on threshold breach; `codeflow budget` CLI for status/policy management
- Non-functional: policy evaluation <2ms; fail-open if policy engine errors; policies hot-reloadable without restart

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → read accumulated cost for {dev, project, team} from tracking.db
    ↓
PolicyEngine.evaluate(context) → Verdict { Allow | Warn(msg) | Downgrade(to_model) | Block(reason) }
    ↓
If Block → return error JSON to agent (tool call rejected)
If Downgrade → rewrite model_id in hook response
If Warn → log warning, allow tool call
    ↓
GovernanceEvent { policy_id, action, reason, budget_remaining, developer_id }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_GOVERNANCE → queued for cloud sync
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add budget check in PreToolUse before command rewrite
- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add query for accumulated cost by dev/project/team/period
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `budget` subcommand
- Create: `src/core/budget_policy.rs` — policy engine: load, evaluate, verdicts
- Create: `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs` — `codeflow budget` CLI
- Create: `data/budget-policy-example.toml` — example policy file

## Implementation Steps

1. **Define policy schema in `data/budget-policy-example.toml`**
   ```toml
   [global]
   period = "monthly"
   warn_at_pct = 75
   block_at_pct = 100

   [[limits]]
   scope = "developer"
   id = "*"
   max_usd = 500.0
   action_on_exceed = "warn"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "project"
   id = "frontend-app"
   max_usd = 2000.0
   action_on_exceed = "downgrade"
   downgrade_to = "claude-haiku-4"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "team"
   id = "platform"
   max_usd = 10000.0
   action_on_exceed = "block"
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/budget_policy.rs`**
   - `struct PolicyConfig` — deserialized from TOML
   - `struct PolicyEngine` — loads config, caches accumulated costs
   - `enum Verdict { Allow, Warn(String), Downgrade(String), Block(String) }`
   - `fn evaluate(&self, dev_id: &str, project: &str, team: &str) -> Verdict`
   - Load policy from: project `.codeflow/budget.toml` → user `~/.config/rtk/budget.toml` → bundled default
   - Accumulated cost query: sum cost_records WHERE scope AND period

3. **Extend PreToolUse in `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - Before command rewrite: run PolicyEngine.evaluate()
   - If Block: return JSON error `{"error": "budget_exceeded", ...}`
   - If Downgrade: modify model_id in response
   - If Warn: write warning to stderr, continue
   - Fail-open on any error

4. **Extend `src/core/tracking.rs`**
   - `fn accumulated_cost(&self, scope: Scope, id: &str, period: Period) -> f64`
   - Index on (scope, period_start) for performance

5. **Create `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow budget status` — current spend vs limits for all scopes
   - `codeflow budget set --scope dev --id alice --max 500` — quick policy update
   - `codeflow budget history` — spending trend with budget overlay
   - `codeflow budget alert --webhook <url>` — configure alert endpoint

6. **Alert system**
   - On threshold breach: POST to webhook URL with JSON payload
   - Use `ureq` (already in deps) for HTTP POST
   - Fire-and-forget: don't block hook on webhook delivery

7. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Budget` variant to Commands enum

8. **Tests**
   - Unit: policy parsing (valid/invalid TOML), verdict evaluation (under/warn/over)
   - Integration: mock PreToolUse with accumulated cost → verify block/downgrade/warn
   - CLI: `codeflow budget status` with fixture policies
   - 10+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Policy TOML parsed correctly with per-dev, per-project, per-team limits
- [ ] PreToolUse blocks tool call when budget exceeded (block action)
- [ ] PreToolUse downgrades model when budget tight (downgrade action)
- [ ] `codeflow budget status` shows current spend vs limits
- [ ] Webhook alerts fire on threshold breach
- [ ] Fail-open: policy engine error → tool call proceeds with warning
- [ ] 10+ new tests

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Blocking tool calls frustrates developers | HIGH | Default to warn-only; block requires explicit opt-in |
| Model downgrade breaks agentic sessions | MEDIUM | Only downgrade for new sessions, not mid-session |
| Cost accumulation query slow with large DB | LOW | Index on (scope, period_start) |

# Phase 3: Budget Governance + Policy Engine

## Overview

Real-time budget enforcement in PreToolUse hooks. Policy engine evaluates per-dev, per-project, per-team spending limits and can warn, downgrade model, or block tool calls that exceed budget.

## Requirements

- Functional: TOML-based policy definitions (per-dev, per-project, per-team limits); PreToolUse budget check (warn/downgrade/block); alert webhooks on threshold breach; `codeflow budget` CLI for status/policy management
- Non-functional: policy evaluation <2ms; fail-open if policy engine errors; policies hot-reloadable without restart

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → read accumulated cost for {dev, project, team} from tracking.db
    ↓
PolicyEngine.evaluate(context) → Verdict { Allow | Warn(msg) | Downgrade(to_model) | Block(reason) }
    ↓
If Block → return error JSON to agent (tool call rejected)
If Downgrade → rewrite model_id in hook response
If Warn → log warning, allow tool call
    ↓
GovernanceEvent { policy_id, action, reason, budget_remaining, developer_id }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_GOVERNANCE → queued for cloud sync
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add budget check in PreToolUse before command rewrite
- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add query for accumulated cost by dev/project/team/period
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `budget` subcommand
- Create: `src/core/budget_policy.rs` — policy engine: load, evaluate, verdicts
- Create: `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs` — `codeflow budget` CLI
- Create: `data/budget-policy-example.toml` — example policy file

## Implementation Steps

1. **Define policy schema in `data/budget-policy-example.toml`**
   ```toml
   [global]
   period = "monthly"
   warn_at_pct = 75
   block_at_pct = 100

   [[limits]]
   scope = "developer"
   id = "*"
   max_usd = 500.0
   action_on_exceed = "warn"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "project"
   id = "frontend-app"
   max_usd = 2000.0
   action_on_exceed = "downgrade"
   downgrade_to = "claude-haiku-4"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "team"
   id = "platform"
   max_usd = 10000.0
   action_on_exceed = "block"
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/budget_policy.rs`**
   - `struct PolicyConfig` — deserialized from TOML
   - `struct PolicyEngine` — loads config, caches accumulated costs
   - `enum Verdict { Allow, Warn(String), Downgrade(String), Block(String) }`
   - `fn evaluate(&self, dev_id: &str, project: &str, team: &str) -> Verdict`
   - Load policy from: project `.codeflow/budget.toml` → user `~/.config/rtk/budget.toml` → bundled default
   - Accumulated cost query: sum cost_records WHERE scope AND period

3. **Extend PreToolUse in `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - Before command rewrite: run PolicyEngine.evaluate()
   - If Block: return JSON error `{"error": "budget_exceeded", ...}`
   - If Downgrade: modify model_id in response
   - If Warn: write warning to stderr, continue
   - Fail-open on any error

4. **Extend `src/core/tracking.rs`**
   - `fn accumulated_cost(&self, scope: Scope, id: &str, period: Period) -> f64`
   - Index on (scope, period_start) for performance

5. **Create `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow budget status` — current spend vs limits for all scopes
   - `codeflow budget set --scope dev --id alice --max 500` — quick policy update
   - `codeflow budget history` — spending trend with budget overlay
   - `codeflow budget alert --webhook <url>` — configure alert endpoint

6. **Alert system**
   - On threshold breach: POST to webhook URL with JSON payload
   - Use `ureq` (already in deps) for HTTP POST
   - Fire-and-forget: don't block hook on webhook delivery

7. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Budget` variant to Commands enum

8. **Tests**
   - Unit: policy parsing (valid/invalid TOML), verdict evaluation (under/warn/over)
   - Integration: mock PreToolUse with accumulated cost → verify block/downgrade/warn
   - CLI: `codeflow budget status` with fixture policies
   - 10+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Policy TOML parsed correctly with per-dev, per-project, per-team limits
- [ ] PreToolUse blocks tool call when budget exceeded (block action)
- [ ] PreToolUse downgrades model when budget tight (downgrade action)
- [ ] `codeflow budget status` shows current spend vs limits
- [ ] Webhook alerts fire on threshold breach
- [ ] Fail-open: policy engine error → tool call proceeds with warning
- [ ] 10+ new tests

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Blocking tool calls frustrates developers | HIGH | Default to warn-only; block requires explicit opt-in |
| Model downgrade breaks agentic sessions | MEDIUM | Only downgrade for new sessions, not mid-session |
| Cost accumulation query slow with large DB | LOW | Index on (scope, period_start) |
