# Phase 3: Budget Governance + Policy Engine

## Overview

Real-time budget enforcement in PreToolUse hooks. Policy engine evaluates per-dev, per-project, per-team spending limits and can warn, downgrade model, or block tool calls that exceed budget.

## Requirements

- Functional: TOML-based policy definitions (per-dev, per-project, per-team limits); PreToolUse budget check (warn/downgrade/block); alert webhooks on threshold breach; `codeflow budget` CLI for status/policy management
- Non-functional: policy evaluation <2ms; fail-open if policy engine errors; policies hot-reloadable without restart

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → read accumulated cost for {dev, project, team} from tracking.db
    ↓
PolicyEngine.evaluate(context) → Verdict { Allow | Warn(msg) | Downgrade(to_model) | Block(reason) }
    ↓
If Block → return error JSON to agent (tool call rejected)
If Downgrade → rewrite model_id in hook response
If Warn → log warning, allow tool call
    ↓
GovernanceEvent { policy_id, action, reason, budget_remaining, developer_id }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_GOVERNANCE → queued for cloud sync
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add budget check in PreToolUse before command rewrite
- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add query for accumulated cost by dev/project/team/period
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `budget` subcommand
- Create: `src/core/budget_policy.rs` — policy engine: load, evaluate, verdicts
- Create: `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs` — `codeflow budget` CLI
- Create: `data/budget-policy-example.toml` — example policy file

## Implementation Steps

1. **Define policy schema in `data/budget-policy-example.toml`**
   ```toml
   [global]
   period = "monthly"
   warn_at_pct = 75
   block_at_pct = 100

   [[limits]]
   scope = "developer"
   id = "*"
   max_usd = 500.0
   action_on_exceed = "warn"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "project"
   id = "frontend-app"
   max_usd = 2000.0
   action_on_exceed = "downgrade"
   downgrade_to = "claude-haiku-4"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "team"
   id = "platform"
   max_usd = 10000.0
   action_on_exceed = "block"
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/budget_policy.rs`**
   - `struct PolicyConfig` — deserialized from TOML
   - `struct PolicyEngine` — loads config, caches accumulated costs
   - `enum Verdict { Allow, Warn(String), Downgrade(String), Block(String) }`
   - `fn evaluate(&self, dev_id: &str, project: &str, team: &str) -> Verdict`
   - Load policy from: project `.codeflow/budget.toml` → user `~/.config/rtk/budget.toml` → bundled default
   - Accumulated cost query: sum cost_records WHERE scope AND period

3. **Extend PreToolUse in `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - Before command rewrite: run PolicyEngine.evaluate()
   - If Block: return JSON error `{"error": "budget_exceeded", ...}`
   - If Downgrade: modify model_id in response
   - If Warn: write warning to stderr, continue
   - Fail-open on any error

4. **Extend `src/core/tracking.rs`**
   - `fn accumulated_cost(&self, scope: Scope, id: &str, period: Period) -> f64`
   - Index on (scope, period_start) for performance

5. **Create `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow budget status` — current spend vs limits for all scopes
   - `codeflow budget set --scope dev --id alice --max 500` — quick policy update
   - `codeflow budget history` — spending trend with budget overlay
   - `codeflow budget alert --webhook <url>` — configure alert endpoint

6. **Alert system**
   - On threshold breach: POST to webhook URL with JSON payload
   - Use `ureq` (already in deps) for HTTP POST
   - Fire-and-forget: don't block hook on webhook delivery

7. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Budget` variant to Commands enum

8. **Tests**
   - Unit: policy parsing (valid/invalid TOML), verdict evaluation (under/warn/over)
   - Integration: mock PreToolUse with accumulated cost → verify block/downgrade/warn
   - CLI: `codeflow budget status` with fixture policies
   - 10+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Policy TOML parsed correctly with per-dev, per-project, per-team limits
- [ ] PreToolUse blocks tool call when budget exceeded (block action)
- [ ] PreToolUse downgrades model when budget tight (downgrade action)
- [ ] `codeflow budget status` shows current spend vs limits
- [ ] Webhook alerts fire on threshold breach
- [ ] Fail-open: policy engine error → tool call proceeds with warning
- [ ] 10+ new tests

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Blocking tool calls frustrates developers | HIGH | Default to warn-only; block requires explicit opt-in |
| Model downgrade breaks agentic sessions | MEDIUM | Only downgrade for new sessions, not mid-session |
| Cost accumulation query slow with large DB | LOW | Index on (scope, period_start) |

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\ck-plan # Planning Create detailed technical implementation plans through research, codebase analysis, solution design, and comprehensive documentation. ## Prerequisites - **ClaudeKit CLI required:** This skill requires `ck` CLI for plan operations. Run `npm install -g claudekit` if not installed. ## CLI Integration This skill orchestrates planning, but ClaudeKit CLI now owns the plan file scaffolding and phase state mutations whenever `ck` is available. Use these commands instead of hand-editing CLI-managed plan structure: ```bash ck plan create \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill ck plan create \ --global \ --title "{plan title}" \ --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \ --dir {plan-dir} \ --source skill cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check --start cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan uncheck ck plan status /absolute/path/to/plan.md ck config ui --port 3456 ``` Rules: - Use `ck plan create` to scaffold `plan.md` and `phase-*.md` when the CLI is available. - Default scope is project-local (`./plans/` under the current project). - Global scope is conditional: use `ck plan create --global ...` or fall back to global scope only when no project context exists. - Use `ck plan check` / `ck plan uncheck` for phase status changes. - Do not hand-edit the phases table for status toggles or structural updates when CLI commands are available. - Use the dashboard at `http://localhost:3456/plans` for visual plan management. - **Overwriting phase stub files:** `ck plan create` scaffolds small boilerplate `phase-XX-*.md` stubs. Always **Read the stub before Write** — Claude Code enforces Read-before-Write on existing files; skipping the Read causes the Write to be rejected, wasting the Write's input tokens AND forcing a retry. The stubs are tiny (~15 lines), so the Read cost is trivial. Then Write the full content following the canonical template below. ### Canonical Phase File Template Use this structure when filling each `phase-XX-*.md`. Loaded once with the skill — no per-file Read needed to learn it. Frontmatter fields match the CLI's phase schema; section headers match `documentation-management.md` so phase files stay consistent across plans. ````markdown --- phase: title: "" status: pending # pending | in-progress | completed priority: P2 # P1 | P2 | P3 effort: "" # e.g. "4h", "2d" dependencies: [] # phase IDs this blocks on --- # Phase : ## Overview <1-2 sentences describing what this phase delivers> ## Requirements - Functional: ... - Non-functional: ... ## Architecture ## Related Code Files - Create: `path/...` - Modify: `path/...` - Delete: `path/...` ## Implementation Steps 1. ... 2. ... ## Success Criteria - [ ] ... ## Risk Assessment ```` **IMPORTANT:** Before you start, scan unfinished plans in the active scope first: - Project scope: `./plans/` - Global scope: the configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` If there are relevant plans overlapping your upcoming plan, update them as well. If you're unsure or need more clarifications, use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask the user. ### Scope Selection - **Project scope** is the default whenever the current working tree has project context. - **Global scope** is allowed only when: - the user explicitly asks for it via `--global`, or - there is no project context to anchor a local plan. - **No project context** means no `.git`, `package.json`, or `CLAUDE.md` was found in the ancestor chain. - Keep scope honest in prose and examples: the skill describes CLI-owned behavior, it does not implement scope resolution itself. ### Cross-Plan Dependency Detection During the pre-creation scan, detect and mark blocking relationships between plans: 1. **Scan** — Read `plan.md` frontmatter of each unfinished plan (status != `completed`/`cancelled`) 2. **Compare scope** — Check overlapping files, shared dependencies, same feature area 3. **Classify relationship:** - New plan needs output of existing plan → new plan `blockedBy: [existing-plan-dir]` - New plan changes something existing plan depends on → existing plan `blockedBy: [new-plan-dir]`, new plan `blocks: [existing-plan-dir]` - Cross-scope dependency → use `global:` or `project:` prefixes - Mutual dependency → both plans reference each other in `blockedBy`/`blocks` 4. **Bidirectional update** — When relationship detected, update BOTH `plan.md` files' frontmatter 5. **Ambiguous?** → Use `AskUserQuestion` with header "Plan Dependency", present detected overlap, ask user to confirm relationship type (blocks/blockedBy/none) **Frontmatter fields**: ```yaml blockedBy: [260301-1200-auth-system] # Same-scope dependency blockedBy: [global:260301-1200-auth-system] # Cross-scope dependency blocks: [project:260228-0900-user-dashboard] # Explicit project-scope dependency ``` **Status interaction:** `ck plan status` is the authoritative inspection surface. Same-scope bare refs stay in the current scope; prefixed refs resolve against the explicit project/global root. Missing refs should warn and show `not found`, not hard-fail the plan. ## Default (No Arguments) If invoked with a task description, proceed with planning workflow. If invoked WITHOUT arguments or with unclear intent, use `AskUserQuestion` to present available operations: | Operation | Description | |-----------|-------------| | `(default)` | Create implementation plan for a task | | `archive` | Write journal entry & archive plans | | `red-team` | Adversarial plan review | | `validate` | Critical questions interview | Present as options via `AskUserQuestion` with header "Planning Operation", question "What would you like to do?". ## Workflow Modes Default: auto-detect planning mode (analyze task complexity and pick mode). | Flag | Mode | Research | Red Team | Validation | Cook Flag | |------|------|----------|----------|------------|-----------| | `--auto` | Auto-detect | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode | | `--fast` | Fast | Skip | Skip | Skip | (none) | | `--hard` | Hard | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | (none) | | `--deep` | Deep | 2-3 researchers + per-phase scout | Yes | Yes | (none) | | `--parallel` | Parallel | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | `--parallel` | | `--two` | Two approaches | 2+ researchers | After selection | After selection | (none) | **Composable flags** (combine with any mode): | Flag | Effect | |------|--------| | `--tdd` | Add tests-first structure to each phase for regression-safe refactors | | `--no-tasks` | Skip task hydration | Load: `references/workflow-modes.md` for auto-detection logic, per-mode workflows, context reminders. ## When to Use - Planning new feature implementations - Architecting system designs - Evaluating technical approaches - Creating implementation roadmaps - Breaking down complex requirements ## Core Responsibilities & Rules Always honoring **YAGNI**, **KISS**, and **DRY** principles. **Be honest, be brutal, straight to the point, and be concise.** ### 0. Scope Challenge Load: `references/scope-challenge.md` **Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task (single file fix, <20 word description) ### 1. Research & Analysis Load: `references/research-phase.md` **Skip if:** Fast mode or provided with researcher reports ### 2. Codebase Understanding Load: `references/codebase-understanding.md` **Skip if:** Provided with scout reports ### 3. Solution Design Load: `references/solution-design.md` ### 4. Plan Creation & Organization Load: `references/plan-organization.md` ### 5. Task Breakdown & Output Standards Load: `references/output-standards.md` ## Process Flow (Authoritative) ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Pre-Creation Check] --> B[Cross-Plan Scan] B --> C[Scope Challenge] C --> D[Mode Detection] D -->|fast| E[Skip Research] D -->|hard/deep/parallel/two| F[Spawn Researchers] E --> G[Codebase Analysis] F --> G G --> H[Write Plan via Planner] H --> I{Red Team?} I -->|Yes| J[Red Team Review] I -->|No| K{Validate?} J --> K K -->|Yes| V[Verification Pass] K -->|No| M[Hydrate Tasks] V --> L[Validation Interview] L --> M M --> N[Present Boundary Reminder] N --> P[Post-Plan Handoff
AskUserQuestion: skip gates already auto-run] P --> O[Journal] ``` **This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node. ## Workflow Process 1. **Pre-Creation Check** → Check Plan Context for active/suggested/none 1b. **Cross-Plan Scan** → Scan unfinished plans, detect `blockedBy`/`blocks` relationships, update both plans 1c. **Scope Challenge** → Run Step 0 scope questions, select mode (see `references/scope-challenge.md`) **Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task 2. **Mode Detection** → Auto-detect or use explicit flag (see `workflow-modes.md`) 3. **Research Phase** → Spawn researchers (skip in fast mode) 4. **Codebase Analysis** → Read docs, scout if needed 5. **Plan Documentation** → Write comprehensive plan via planner subagent 6. **Red Team Review** → Run `/ck:plan red-team {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes) 7. **Post-Plan Validation** → Run `/ck:plan validate {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes) 8. **Hydrate Tasks** → Create Claude Tasks from phases (default on, `--no-tasks` to skip) 9. **Boundary Reminder** → Present optional next-step commands with absolute path 10. **Journal** → Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion ### Whole-Plan Consistency Gate This gate is mandatory after `/ck:plan validate` or `/ck:plan red-team` edits any plan file. Load: `references/verification-roles.md` → "Whole-Plan Consistency Sweep". Before recommending `/ck:cook`, re-read `plan.md` and every `phase-*.md` file. Search all plan files for stale terms, rejected assumptions, renamed APIs/files/fields, superseded decisions, and duplicate embedded drafts/contracts. Reconcile contradictions across the entire plan, not only the edited phase. If unresolved contradictions remain, report them and ask the user. Do not recommend cook until the whole-plan consistency sweep reports zero unresolved contradictions. ## Output Requirements **IMPORTANT:** Invoke "/ck:project-organization" skill to organize the outputs. - DO NOT implement code - only create plans - Respond with plan file path and summary - Ensure self-contained plans with necessary context - Include code snippets/pseudocode when clarifying - Fully respect the `./docs/development-rules.md` file ## Task Management Plan files = persistent. Tasks = session-scoped. Hydration bridges the gap. **Default:** Auto-hydrate tasks after plan files are written. Skip with `--no-tasks`. **3-Task Rule:** <3 phases → skip task creation. **Fallback:** Task tools (`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskGet`/`TaskList`) are CLI-only — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for tracking. Plan files remain the source of truth; hydration is an optimization, not a requirement. Load: `references/task-management.md` for hydration pattern, TaskCreate patterns, cook handoff protocol. ### Hydration Workflow 1. Write plan.md + phase files (persistent layer) 2. TaskCreate per phase with `addBlockedBy` chain (skip if Task tools unavailable) 3. TaskCreate for critical/high-risk steps within phases (skip if Task tools unavailable) 4. Metadata: phase, priority, effort, planDir, phaseFile 5. Cook picks up via TaskList (same session) or re-hydrates (new session) ## Active Plan State Check `## Plan Context` injected by hooks: - **"Plan: {path}"** → Active plan. Ask "Continue? [Y/n]" - **"Suggested: {path}"** → Branch hint only. Ask if activate or create new. - **"Plan: none"** → Create new using `Plan dir:` from `## Naming` After creating plan: `node .claude/scripts/set-active-plan.cjs {plan-dir}` Reports: Active plans → plan-specific path. Suggested → default path. ### Important **DO NOT** create plans or reports in arbitrary user directories. **MUST** create plans or reports in one of these allowed roots: - project scope → current working project directory - global scope → configured global plans root - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/` ## Subcommands | Subcommand | Reference | Purpose | |------------|-----------|---------| | `/ck:plan archive` | `references/archive-workflow.md` | Archive plans + write journal entries | | `/ck:plan red-team` | `references/red-team-workflow.md` | Adversarial plan review with hostile reviewers | | `/ck:plan validate` | `references/validate-workflow.md` | Validate plan with critical questions interview | ## Post-Plan Handoff (MANDATORY at session end) After `plan.md` + phase files are written and the user has reviewed/approved them, use `AskUserQuestion` to offer the appropriate next step. Recommend the option that best fits the plan's risk/scope; recommended option listed FIRST and labelled "(Recommended)". | Option | Recommend When | Why | |--------|----------------|-----| | `/ck:plan validate` | Plan is moderate-to-complex; user wants critical-questions interview before implementation | Cheapest gate — surfaces unspecified assumptions, missing acceptance criteria, hand-wavy phases | | `/ck:plan red-team` | Plan touches security, auth, payments, data integrity, public APIs, infra, or has high blast radius | Adversarial reviewers stress-test the plan for failure modes, attack vectors, and missing edge cases | | `/ck:cook ` | Plan is small / well-understood / low-risk and user wants to start implementation | Skip extra gates; go straight to implementation | | End session | User wants to review/share plan before deciding | Stop with plan path returned | **Skip this step ONLY when:** - The current invocation IS already a subcommand (`validate`, `red-team`, `archive`) — those have their own terminal handoff. - User explicitly said "just plan, don't suggest next step". **Skip an individual option ONLY when the active mode already auto-ran that gate (per Workflow Process Steps 6-7):** - Omit `/ck:plan red-team` from the offered options when mode is `--hard`, `--deep`, `--parallel`, or `--two` (Step 6 already ran adversarial review). - Omit `/ck:plan validate` from the offered options when mode is `--deep` (Step 7 already ran validation). - If both gates already ran, the Post-Plan Handoff still fires but offers only `/ck:cook ` and `End session`. After selection: invoke the chosen command with the plan path as argument for continuity. ## Quality Standards - Thorough and specific, consider long-term maintainability - Research thoroughly when uncertain - Address security and performance concerns - Detailed enough for junior developers - Validate against existing codebase patterns **Remember:** Plan quality determines implementation success. Be comprehensive and consider all solution aspects. ## Workflow Position **Typically follows:** `/ck:brainstorm` (after exploring options), `/ck:scout` (after codebase discovery) **May precede:** `/ck:cook` after user approval (otherwise stop with plan path and next-step options) **Related:** `/ck:brainstorm` (explore before planning), `/ck:cook` (execute after planning) ARGUMENTS: red-team plans/260603-codeflow-ai-cost-intelligence-engine/plan.md

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Codebase reality check:** RTK is 105 .rs files, ~69K LOC. Key assets to extend:
- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, token savings, daily/weekly/monthly stats
- `ccusage.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` — Claude Code spending data parsing + economics
- `hooks/` — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook system for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, etc.
- `discover/` — command classification + session analysis
- `filters/` — 65+ TOML-based output filters

**What does NOT exist yet:** protobuf schema, provenance records, signed attestation, budget policy engine, dependency validation, compliance exports, cloud backend (Go), ClickHouse, dashboard (Next.js).

**Target:** 12-week MVP across 7 phases. Phases 1-5 = CLI (Rust). Phase 6 = Cloud. Phase 7 = Launch.

## Brainstorm Source

`brainstorm-final-260606.md` — 3-session brainstorm, verified sources, competitive analysis of 12 competitors, 4-pillar architecture.

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort | Dependencies |
|-------|------|--------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | [Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core](./phase-01-foundation-proto-schema-provenance-core.md) | Pending | 2w | None |
| 2 | [Cost Attribution Engine](./phase-02-cost-attribution-engine.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 3 | [Budget Governance + Policy Engine](./phase-03-budget-governance-policy-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phase 2 |
| 4 | [Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection](./phase-04-quality-gate-dependency-hallucination-detection.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 5 | [Compliance Export Engine](./phase-05-compliance-export-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phases 1-4 |
| 6 | [Cloud Backend + Dashboard](./phase-06-cloud-backend-dashboard.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 5 |
| 7 | [OSS Polish + Launch Prep](./phase-07-oss-polish-launch-prep.md) | Pending | 1w | Phase 6 |

**Parallelism:** Phases 2-3 (cost) and Phase 4 (quality) can run in parallel after Phase 1.

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral (Rust CLI ↔ Go cloud)
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **SQLite (WAL mode) for local** — already proven in tracking.rs, extend for provenance/cost
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop
5. **blake3 for content hashing** — fastest cryptographic hash, already in Rust ecosystem

## Risk Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Hook API changes (Claude Code, Cursor) | Multi-agent support already in RTK; abstract hook interface |
| Protobuf adds build complexity | Use `prost` crate with build.rs; proto files in `proto/` dir |
| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine, optional org-managed keys later |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode + connection pooling (already used in tracking.rs) |

## Dependencies

- `prost` + `prost-build` — protobuf for Rust
- `ed25519-dalek` — Ed25519 signatures
- `blake3` — content hashing
- `ureq` — HTTP client (already in Cargo.toml)
- `serde_json` — JSON (already in Cargo.toml)

10	# Phase 1: Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core
11	
12	## Overview
13	
14	Establish event schema (protobuf), content hashing (blake3), signed attestation (Ed25519), and the `codeflow blame` CLI command. This phase creates the data foundation all other pillars depend on.
15	
16	## Requirements
17	
18	- Functional: capture model_id, prompt hash, code hash, file paths, contributor type at point-of-generation via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; sign provenance records with Ed25519; export Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON; `codeflow blame` command shows line-by-line AI attribution
19	- Non-functional: <5ms hook latency (fail-open); provenance DB <50MB for 90 days typical usage; zero network dependency for local operation
20	
21	## Architecture
22	
23	```
24	PreToolUse hook → extract model_id, prompt context
25	    ↓
26	PostToolUse hook → capture file diffs, compute blake3 hash
27	    ↓
28	ProvenanceRecord { model_id, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
29	    ↓
30	SQLite (provenance.db, WAL mode) ← stores locally
31	    ↓
32	Protobuf event → EVENT_TYPE_PROVENANCE → queued for cloud sync (Phase 6)
33	```
34	
35	**Key decision:** Extend existing `hooks/hook_cmd.rs` PreToolUse/PostToolUse flow. Currently RTK hooks rewrite Bash commands. New hooks capture provenance metadata from the same JSON stdin without interfering with rewrite logic.
36	
37	## Related Code Files
38	
39	- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add provenance capture to PreToolUse/PostToolUse handlers
40	- Modify: `src/hooks/mod.rs` — export new provenance module
41	- Modify: `src/core/mod.rs` — export provenance module
42	- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `blame` subcommand
43	- Modify: `Cargo.toml` — add prost, prost-build, ed25519-dalek, blake3 deps
44	- Create: `proto/events.proto` — protobuf schema for all 7 event types
45	- Create: `build.rs` — prost-build compilation of proto files
46	- Create: `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord struct, signing, storage
47	- Create: `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management, sign/verify
48	- Create: `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 hashing for code content
49	- Create: `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export format
50	- Create: `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs` — `codeflow blame` command implementation
51	
52	## Implementation Steps
53	
54	1. **Add dependencies to Cargo.toml**
55	   - `prost = "0.13"`, `prost-types = "0.13"` (runtime)
56	   - `prost-build = "0.13"` (build-dependency)
57	   - `ed25519-dalek = { version = "2", features = ["rand_core"] }`
58	   - `blake3 = "1"`
59	   - `rand = "0.8"` (for key generation)
60	
61	2. **Create `proto/events.proto`**
62	   - Define EventType enum (7 types per brainstorm §3.4)
63	   - Define ProvenanceEvent, CostEvent, GovernanceEvent, QualityEvent messages
64	   - Define EventEnvelope wrapper with timestamp, event_type, oneof payload
65	
66	3. **Create `build.rs`**
67	   - Use prost-build to compile proto/events.proto → src/proto/mod.rs
68	   - Add to .gitignore: generated proto output (or check in — decide)
69	
70	4. **Create `src/core/content_hash.rs`**
71	   - `fn hash_content(content: &[u8]) -> String` — blake3 hash, hex-encoded
72	   - `fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — hash file contents
73	   - `fn hash_diff(old: &str, new: &str) -> String` — hash the diff
74	
75	5. **Create `src/core/attestation.rs`**
76	   - `struct KeyPair` — wraps Ed25519 keypair
77	   - `fn generate_keypair() -> KeyPair` — auto-generate, store at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
78	   - `fn load_or_generate() -> Result<KeyPair>` — lazy init
79	   - `fn sign(keypair: &KeyPair, data: &[u8]) -> String` — hex-encoded signature
80	   - `fn verify(pubkey: &[u8], data: &[u8], sig: &str) -> bool`
81	
82	6. **Create `src/core/provenance.rs`**
83	   - `struct ProvenanceRecord` — model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, start_line, end_line, contributor_type (human|ai|mixed|unknown), attestation_sig, timestamp, developer_id, session_id
84	   - `struct ProvenanceStore` — SQLite-backed (new DB file `provenance.db` or extend `tracking.db`)
85	   - `fn record_provenance(...)` — insert record + sign with attestation
86	   - `fn query_by_file(path: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>` — for blame command
87	   - `fn query_by_session(session_id: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>`
88	   - Schema: `CREATE TABLE provenance_records (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT, ...)`
89	
90	7. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
91	   - In PreToolUse handler: extract `model_id` from JSON context (Claude Code sends session info)
92	   - In PostToolUse handler: if tool was file-write/edit, compute blake3 hash of changed content
93	   - Create ProvenanceRecord, sign, store in provenance DB
94	   - Fail-open: if provenance capture fails, log warning but don't block the tool call
95	
96	8. **Create `src/core/agent_trace.rs`**
97	   - Implement Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON format (per github.com/cursor/agent-trace spec)
98	   - `fn to_agent_trace(record: &ProvenanceRecord) -> Value` — convert to spec JSON
99	   - `fn export_agent_trace(records: Vec<ProvenanceRecord>) -> String` — full trace file
100	
101	9. **Create `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs`**
102	   - `codeflow blame <file>` — line-by-line attribution
103	   - Output format: `<line_num> | <contributor> | <model_id> | <timestamp> | <code>`
104	   - Color-coded: human=green, ai=yellow, mixed=cyan, unknown=gray
105	   - Flag: `--json` for machine-readable output
106	   - Flag: `--session <id>` to filter by session
107	
108	10. **Wire into main.rs**
109	    - Add `Blame` variant to Commands enum
110	    - Route to blame_cmd handler
111	
112	11. **Tests**
113	    - Unit: content_hash (known vectors), attestation (sign/verify roundtrip), provenance (CRUD)
114	    - Integration: mock PreToolUse/PostToolUse JSON → verify provenance record created
115	    - CLI: `codeflow blame` on test fixture files
116	
117	## Success Criteria
118	
119	- [ ] `proto/events.proto` compiles with prost-build, generates Rust types
120	- [ ] Ed25519 keypair auto-generated on first use, persisted at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
121	- [ ] ProvenanceRecord created for every PostToolUse file-write event
122	- [ ] `codeflow blame <file>` shows line-by-line AI attribution with model_id
123	- [ ] Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export passes format validation
124	- [ ] Hook latency remains <5ms (benchmark test)
125	- [ ] Existing RTK tests still pass (no regression)
126	- [ ] 15+ new tests for provenance, attestation, content_hash, blame
127	
128	## Risk Assessment
129	
130	| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
131	|------|----------|------------|
132	| Claude Code doesn't expose model_id in hook JSON | HIGH | Parse from session metadata; fallback to "unknown" with flag |
133	| prost-build adds Windows build complexity | MEDIUM | Use pre-generated .rs files as fallback; CI builds on Linux |
134	| Provenance DB grows too large | LOW | 90-day retention (reuse tracking.rs pattern); vacuum on startup |
135	
136	## Security Considerations
137	
138	- Ed25519 private key stored with 0600 permissions (Unix) or ACL-restricted (Windows)

# Phase 1: Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core

## Overview

Establish event schema (protobuf), content hashing (blake3), signed attestation (Ed25519), and the `codeflow blame` CLI command. This phase creates the data foundation all other pillars depend on.

## Requirements

- Functional: capture model_id, prompt hash, code hash, file paths, contributor type at point-of-generation via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; sign provenance records with Ed25519; export Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON; `codeflow blame` command shows line-by-line AI attribution
- Non-functional: <5ms hook latency (fail-open); provenance DB <50MB for 90 days typical usage; zero network dependency for local operation

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → extract model_id, prompt context
    ↓
PostToolUse hook → capture file diffs, compute blake3 hash
    ↓
ProvenanceRecord { model_id, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
    ↓
SQLite (provenance.db, WAL mode) ← stores locally
    ↓
Protobuf event → EVENT_TYPE_PROVENANCE → queued for cloud sync (Phase 6)
```

**Key decision:** Extend existing `hooks/hook_cmd.rs` PreToolUse/PostToolUse flow. Currently RTK hooks rewrite Bash commands. New hooks capture provenance metadata from the same JSON stdin without interfering with rewrite logic.

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add provenance capture to PreToolUse/PostToolUse handlers
- Modify: `src/hooks/mod.rs` — export new provenance module
- Modify: `src/core/mod.rs` — export provenance module
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `blame` subcommand
- Modify: `Cargo.toml` — add prost, prost-build, ed25519-dalek, blake3 deps
- Create: `proto/events.proto` — protobuf schema for all 7 event types
- Create: `build.rs` — prost-build compilation of proto files
- Create: `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord struct, signing, storage
- Create: `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management, sign/verify
- Create: `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 hashing for code content
- Create: `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export format
- Create: `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs` — `codeflow blame` command implementation

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add dependencies to Cargo.toml**
   - `prost = "0.13"`, `prost-types = "0.13"` (runtime)
   - `prost-build = "0.13"` (build-dependency)
   - `ed25519-dalek = { version = "2", features = ["rand_core"] }`
   - `blake3 = "1"`
   - `rand = "0.8"` (for key generation)

2. **Create `proto/events.proto`**
   - Define EventType enum (7 types per brainstorm §3.4)
   - Define ProvenanceEvent, CostEvent, GovernanceEvent, QualityEvent messages
   - Define EventEnvelope wrapper with timestamp, event_type, oneof payload

3. **Create `build.rs`**
   - Use prost-build to compile proto/events.proto → src/proto/mod.rs
   - Add to .gitignore: generated proto output (or check in — decide)

4. **Create `src/core/content_hash.rs`**
   - `fn hash_content(content: &[u8]) -> String` — blake3 hash, hex-encoded
   - `fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — hash file contents
   - `fn hash_diff(old: &str, new: &str) -> String` — hash the diff

5. **Create `src/core/attestation.rs`**
   - `struct KeyPair` — wraps Ed25519 keypair
   - `fn generate_keypair() -> KeyPair` — auto-generate, store at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
   - `fn load_or_generate() -> Result<KeyPair>` — lazy init
   - `fn sign(keypair: &KeyPair, data: &[u8]) -> String` — hex-encoded signature
   - `fn verify(pubkey: &[u8], data: &[u8], sig: &str) -> bool`

6. **Create `src/core/provenance.rs`**
   - `struct ProvenanceRecord` — model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, start_line, end_line, contributor_type (human|ai|mixed|unknown), attestation_sig, timestamp, developer_id, session_id
   - `struct ProvenanceStore` — SQLite-backed (new DB file `provenance.db` or extend `tracking.db`)
   - `fn record_provenance(...)` — insert record + sign with attestation
   - `fn query_by_file(path: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>` — for blame command
   - `fn query_by_session(session_id: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>`
   - Schema: `CREATE TABLE provenance_records (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT, ...)`

7. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - In PreToolUse handler: extract `model_id` from JSON context (Claude Code sends session info)
   - In PostToolUse handler: if tool was file-write/edit, compute blake3 hash of changed content
   - Create ProvenanceRecord, sign, store in provenance DB
   - Fail-open: if provenance capture fails, log warning but don't block the tool call

8. **Create `src/core/agent_trace.rs`**
   - Implement Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON format (per github.com/cursor/agent-trace spec)
   - `fn to_agent_trace(record: &ProvenanceRecord) -> Value` — convert to spec JSON
   - `fn export_agent_trace(records: Vec<ProvenanceRecord>) -> String` — full trace file

9. **Create `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow blame <file>` — line-by-line attribution
   - Output format: `<line_num> | <contributor> | <model_id> | <timestamp> | <code>`
   - Color-coded: human=green, ai=yellow, mixed=cyan, unknown=gray
   - Flag: `--json` for machine-readable output
   - Flag: `--session <id>` to filter by session

10. **Wire into main.rs**
    - Add `Blame` variant to Commands enum
    - Route to blame_cmd handler

11. **Tests**
    - Unit: content_hash (known vectors), attestation (sign/verify roundtrip), provenance (CRUD)
    - Integration: mock PreToolUse/PostToolUse JSON → verify provenance record created
    - CLI: `codeflow blame` on test fixture files

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `proto/events.proto` compiles with prost-build, generates Rust types
- [ ] Ed25519 keypair auto-generated on first use, persisted at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
- [ ] ProvenanceRecord created for every PostToolUse file-write event
- [ ] `codeflow blame <file>` shows line-by-line AI attribution with model_id
- [ ] Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export passes format validation
- [ ] Hook latency remains <5ms (benchmark test)
- [ ] Existing RTK tests still pass (no regression)
- [ ] 15+ new tests for provenance, attestation, content_hash, blame

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Claude Code doesn't expose model_id in hook JSON | HIGH | Parse from session metadata; fallback to "unknown" with flag |
| prost-build adds Windows build complexity | MEDIUM | Use pre-generated .rs files as fallback; CI builds on Linux |
| Provenance DB grows too large | LOW | 90-day retention (reuse tracking.rs pattern); vacuum on startup |

## Security Considerations

- Ed25519 private key stored with 0600 permissions (Unix) or ACL-restricted (Windows)
- Never log private key material
- Attestation signatures are non-repudiable — document this for users
- Content hashes use blake3 (cryptographic) not xxhash (fast but not cryptographic)

# CODEFLOW — AI Code Supply Chain OS

## Overview

Transform RTK (`D:/code/invesments/tools_decisions/rtk-analysis/`) from a token compression CLI into an **AI Code Supply Chain Operating System** answering 4 questions: WHO wrote it, WHAT did it cost, IS it safe, CAN you prove it.

**Codebase reality check:** RTK is 105 .rs files, ~69K LOC. Key assets to extend:
- `tracking.rs` (1689 LOC) — SQLite tracking, token savings, daily/weekly/monthly stats
- `ccusage.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` — Claude Code spending data parsing + economics
- `hooks/` — PreToolUse/PostToolUse hook system for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, etc.
- `discover/` — command classification + session analysis
- `filters/` — 65+ TOML-based output filters

**What does NOT exist yet:** protobuf schema, provenance records, signed attestation, budget policy engine, dependency validation, compliance exports, cloud backend (Go), ClickHouse, dashboard (Next.js).

**Target:** 12-week MVP across 7 phases. Phases 1-5 = CLI (Rust). Phase 6 = Cloud. Phase 7 = Launch.

## Brainstorm Source

`brainstorm-final-260606.md` — 3-session brainstorm, verified sources, competitive analysis of 12 competitors, 4-pillar architecture.

## Phases

| Phase | Name | Status | Effort | Dependencies |
|-------|------|--------|--------|--------------|
| 1 | [Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core](./phase-01-foundation-proto-schema-provenance-core.md) | Pending | 2w | None |
| 2 | [Cost Attribution Engine](./phase-02-cost-attribution-engine.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 3 | [Budget Governance + Policy Engine](./phase-03-budget-governance-policy-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phase 2 |
| 4 | [Quality Gate — Dependency + Hallucination Detection](./phase-04-quality-gate-dependency-hallucination-detection.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 1 |
| 5 | [Compliance Export Engine](./phase-05-compliance-export-engine.md) | Pending | 1.5w | Phases 1-4 |
| 6 | [Cloud Backend + Dashboard](./phase-06-cloud-backend-dashboard.md) | Pending | 2w | Phase 5 |
| 7 | [OSS Polish + Launch Prep](./phase-07-oss-polish-launch-prep.md) | Pending | 1w | Phase 6 |

**Parallelism:** Phases 2-3 (cost) and Phase 4 (quality) can run in parallel after Phase 1.

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral (Rust CLI ↔ Go cloud)
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **SQLite (WAL mode) for local** — already proven in tracking.rs, extend for provenance/cost
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop
5. **blake3 for content hashing** — fastest cryptographic hash, already in Rust ecosystem

## Risk Mitigations

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Hook API changes (Claude Code, Cursor) | Multi-agent support already in RTK; abstract hook interface |
| Protobuf adds build complexity | Use `prost` crate with build.rs; proto files in `proto/` dir |
| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine, optional org-managed keys later |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode + connection pooling (already used in tracking.rs) |

## Dependencies

- `prost` + `prost-build` — protobuf for Rust
- `ed25519-dalek` — Ed25519 signatures
- `blake3` — content hashing
- `ureq` — HTTP client (already in Cargo.toml)
- `serde_json` — JSON (already in Cargo.toml)

## Key Architecture Decisions

1. **Protobuf for events** — structured, versionable, language-neutral
2. **Ed25519 for attestation** — fast, small signatures, no certificate infra needed
3. **Single SQLite DB (extend tracking.db)** — no split-brain risk; single WAL, single retention, single backup
4. **Agent Trace v0.1.0 compat** — implement spec for Cursor/Devin/Cloudflare/Vercel interop

8. **Warn/Block only** — no model Downgrade verdict (hook protocol doesn't support model_id in response)
9. **Cross-platform key storage** — use `dirs::data_dir()` (dirs crate already in deps), not Linux-only `~/.local/share/`
10. **Verify name availability early** — check `codeflow` on crates.io, npm, Homebrew, domain before Phase 1

| Risk | Mitigation |
|------|------------|
| Hook API changes (Claude Code, Cursor) | Multi-agent support already in RTK; abstract hook interface |
| Protobuf adds build complexity | Use `prost` crate; extend existing build.rs (DO NOT create new) |
| Ed25519 key management | Auto-generate per-machine via `dirs::data_dir()` (cross-platform) |
| SQLite concurrency under heavy sessions | WAL mode; single connection (no pooling — tracking.rs uses single conn) |
| PostToolUse doesn't exist | Git-diff provenance capture on PreToolUse of NEXT tool call; file watcher fallback |
| model_id not in hook JSON | Enrich from ccusage session data retroactively; fallback "unknown" |
| Budget enforcement bypassable | Document as local-first limitation; real enforcement requires API key proxy (future cloud) |

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → extract model_id, prompt context
    ↓
PostToolUse hook → capture file diffs, compute blake3 hash
    ↓
ProvenanceRecord { model_id, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
    ↓
SQLite (provenance.db, WAL mode) ← stores locally
    ↓

# Phase 1: Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core

## Overview

Establish event schema (protobuf), content hashing (blake3), signed attestation (Ed25519), and the `codeflow blame` CLI command. This phase creates the data foundation all other pillars depend on.

## Requirements

- Functional: capture model_id, prompt hash, code hash, file paths, contributor type at point-of-generation via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; sign provenance records with Ed25519; export Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON; `codeflow blame` command shows line-by-line AI attribution
- Non-functional: <5ms hook latency (fail-open); provenance DB <50MB for 90 days typical usage; zero network dependency for local operation

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → extract model_id, prompt context
    ↓
PostToolUse hook → capture file diffs, compute blake3 hash
    ↓
ProvenanceRecord { model_id, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
    ↓
SQLite (provenance.db, WAL mode) ← stores locally
    ↓
Protobuf event → EVENT_TYPE_PROVENANCE → queued for cloud sync (Phase 6)
```

**Key decision:** Extend existing `hooks/hook_cmd.rs` PreToolUse/PostToolUse flow. Currently RTK hooks rewrite Bash commands. New hooks capture provenance metadata from the same JSON stdin without interfering with rewrite logic.

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add provenance capture to PreToolUse/PostToolUse handlers
- Modify: `src/hooks/mod.rs` — export new provenance module
- Modify: `src/core/mod.rs` — export provenance module
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `blame` subcommand
- Modify: `Cargo.toml` — add prost, prost-build, ed25519-dalek, blake3 deps
- Create: `proto/events.proto` — protobuf schema for all 7 event types
- Create: `build.rs` — prost-build compilation of proto files
- Create: `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord struct, signing, storage
- Create: `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management, sign/verify
- Create: `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 hashing for code content
- Create: `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export format
- Create: `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs` — `codeflow blame` command implementation

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add dependencies to Cargo.toml**
   - `prost = "0.13"`, `prost-types = "0.13"` (runtime)
   - `prost-build = "0.13"` (build-dependency)
   - `ed25519-dalek = { version = "2", features = ["rand_core"] }`
   - `blake3 = "1"`
   - `rand = "0.8"` (for key generation)

2. **Create `proto/events.proto`**
   - Define EventType enum (7 types per brainstorm §3.4)
   - Define ProvenanceEvent, CostEvent, GovernanceEvent, QualityEvent messages
   - Define EventEnvelope wrapper with timestamp, event_type, oneof payload

3. **Create `build.rs`**
   - Use prost-build to compile proto/events.proto → src/proto/mod.rs
   - Add to .gitignore: generated proto output (or check in — decide)

4. **Create `src/core/content_hash.rs`**
   - `fn hash_content(content: &[u8]) -> String` — blake3 hash, hex-encoded
   - `fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — hash file contents
   - `fn hash_diff(old: &str, new: &str) -> String` — hash the diff

5. **Create `src/core/attestation.rs`**
   - `struct KeyPair` — wraps Ed25519 keypair
   - `fn generate_keypair() -> KeyPair` — auto-generate, store at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
   - `fn load_or_generate() -> Result<KeyPair>` — lazy init
   - `fn sign(keypair: &KeyPair, data: &[u8]) -> String` — hex-encoded signature
   - `fn verify(pubkey: &[u8], data: &[u8], sig: &str) -> bool`

6. **Create `src/core/provenance.rs`**
   - `struct ProvenanceRecord` — model_id, model_version, prompt_hash, code_hash, file_path, start_line, end_line, contributor_type (human|ai|mixed|unknown), attestation_sig, timestamp, developer_id, session_id
   - `struct ProvenanceStore` — SQLite-backed (new DB file `provenance.db` or extend `tracking.db`)
   - `fn record_provenance(...)` — insert record + sign with attestation
   - `fn query_by_file(path: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>` — for blame command
   - `fn query_by_session(session_id: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>`
   - Schema: `CREATE TABLE provenance_records (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT, ...)`

7. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - In PreToolUse handler: extract `model_id` from JSON context (Claude Code sends session info)
   - In PostToolUse handler: if tool was file-write/edit, compute blake3 hash of changed content
   - Create ProvenanceRecord, sign, store in provenance DB
   - Fail-open: if provenance capture fails, log warning but don't block the tool call

8. **Create `src/core/agent_trace.rs`**
   - Implement Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON format (per github.com/cursor/agent-trace spec)
   - `fn to_agent_trace(record: &ProvenanceRecord) -> Value` — convert to spec JSON
   - `fn export_agent_trace(records: Vec<ProvenanceRecord>) -> String` — full trace file

9. **Create `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow blame <file>` — line-by-line attribution
   - Output format: `<line_num> | <contributor> | <model_id> | <timestamp> | <code>`
   - Color-coded: human=green, ai=yellow, mixed=cyan, unknown=gray
   - Flag: `--json` for machine-readable output
   - Flag: `--session <id>` to filter by session

10. **Wire into main.rs**
    - Add `Blame` variant to Commands enum
    - Route to blame_cmd handler

11. **Tests**
    - Unit: content_hash (known vectors), attestation (sign/verify roundtrip), provenance (CRUD)
    - Integration: mock PreToolUse/PostToolUse JSON → verify provenance record created
    - CLI: `codeflow blame` on test fixture files

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `proto/events.proto` compiles with prost-build, generates Rust types
- [ ] Ed25519 keypair auto-generated on first use, persisted at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
- [ ] ProvenanceRecord created for every PostToolUse file-write event
- [ ] `codeflow blame <file>` shows line-by-line AI attribution with model_id
- [ ] Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export passes format validation
- [ ] Hook latency remains <5ms (benchmark test)
- [ ] Existing RTK tests still pass (no regression)
- [ ] 15+ new tests for provenance, attestation, content_hash, blame

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Claude Code doesn't expose model_id in hook JSON | HIGH | Parse from session metadata; fallback to "unknown" with flag |
| prost-build adds Windows build complexity | MEDIUM | Use pre-generated .rs files as fallback; CI builds on Linux |
| Provenance DB grows too large | LOW | 90-day retention (reuse tracking.rs pattern); vacuum on startup |

## Security Considerations

- Ed25519 private key stored with 0600 permissions (Unix) or ACL-restricted (Windows)
- Never log private key material
- Attestation signatures are non-repudiable — document this for users
- Content hashes use blake3 (cryptographic) not xxhash (fast but not cryptographic)

# Phase 1: Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core

## Overview

Establish event schema (protobuf), content hashing (blake3), signed attestation (Ed25519), and the `codeflow blame` CLI command. This phase creates the data foundation all other pillars depend on.

## Requirements

- Functional: capture model_id, prompt hash, code hash, file paths, contributor type at point-of-generation via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; sign provenance records with Ed25519; export Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON; `codeflow blame` command shows line-by-line AI attribution
- Non-functional: <5ms hook latency (fail-open); provenance DB <50MB for 90 days typical usage; zero network dependency for local operation

## Architecture

**Critical constraint:** Only PreToolUse hooks exist. PostToolUse does NOT exist in any agent's hook protocol. Each hook invocation is a separate OS process — no shared in-memory state. Hook JSON payload contains only `tool_name` + `tool_input.command` — no `model_id`.

```
PreToolUse hook (tool N) → snapshot working tree state (file hashes)
    ↓ (agent executes tool, modifies files)
PreToolUse hook (tool N+1) → diff working tree vs snapshot → detect changes from tool N
    ↓
ProvenanceRecord { model_id: "unknown"/enriched, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db, WAL mode) ← single DB, no split-brain
    ↓
Protobuf event → EVENT_TYPE_PROVENANCE → queued for export
```

**Provenance capture strategy:** Since PostToolUse doesn't exist, use "diff-on-next-PreToolUse" pattern:
1. Each PreToolUse: read last snapshot from DB, diff current working tree against it, record changes as provenance from previous tool call
2. Store new snapshot for next comparison
3. Fallback: `codeflow blame --retroactive` scans git history for attribution after the fact

**model_id enrichment:** Hook JSON has no model_id. Strategies:
1. Parse from ccusage session data (retroactive, but accurate)
2. Infer from agent config files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/config.json`)
3. Accept "unknown" as valid — enrich later when data available

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add provenance snapshot capture to PreToolUse handlers (no PostToolUse exists)
- Modify: `src/hooks/mod.rs` — export new provenance module

- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `blame` subcommand
- Modify: `Cargo.toml` — add prost, prost-build, ed25519-dalek, blake3 deps
- Create: `proto/events.proto` — protobuf schema for all 7 event types
- Modify: `build.rs` — extend existing build.rs with prost-build compilation of proto files (DO NOT create new — existing handles Windows stack size + TOML filter concat)
- Create: `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord struct, signing, storage
- Create: `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management, sign/verify
- Create: `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 hashing for code content
- Create: `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export format
- Create: `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs` — `codeflow blame` command implementation

   - `blake3 = "1"`
   - `rand = "0.8"` (for key generation)

2. **Create `proto/events.proto`**
   - Define EventType enum (7 types per brainstorm §3.4)
   - Define ProvenanceEvent, CostEvent, GovernanceEvent, QualityEvent messages
   - Define EventEnvelope wrapper with timestamp, event_type, oneof payload

3. **Extend existing `build.rs`** (66 LOC — has Windows `/STACK:8388608` + TOML filter concat)
   - Add prost-build to compile proto/events.proto → src/proto/mod.rs
   - Preserve existing Windows stack size config and filter concatenation logic
   - Add to .gitignore: generated proto output (or check in — decide)

4. **Create `src/core/content_hash.rs`**
   - `fn hash_content(content: &[u8]) -> String` — blake3 hash, hex-encoded
   - `fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — hash file contents
   - `fn hash_diff(old: &str, new: &str) -> String` — hash the diff

5. **Create `src/core/attestation.rs`**
   - `struct KeyPair` — wraps Ed25519 keypair
   - `fn generate_keypair() -> KeyPair` — auto-generate, store at `dirs::data_dir()/rtk/keys/` (cross-platform via `dirs` crate, already in Cargo.toml)
   - `fn load_or_generate() -> Result<KeyPair>` — lazy init
   - `fn sign(keypair: &KeyPair, data: &[u8]) -> String` — hex-encoded signature
   - `fn verify(pubkey: &[u8], data: &[u8], sig: &str) -> bool`

   - `struct ProvenanceStore` — SQLite-backed (new DB file `provenance.db` or extend `tracking.db`)
   - `fn record_provenance(...)` — insert record + sign with attestation
   - `fn query_by_file(path: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>` — for blame command
   - `fn query_by_session(session_id: &str) -> Vec<ProvenanceRecord>`
   - Schema: `CREATE TABLE provenance_records (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, model_id TEXT, ...)`

7. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - In PreToolUse handler: extract `model_id` from JSON context (Claude Code sends session info)
   - In PostToolUse handler: if tool was file-write/edit, compute blake3 hash of changed content
   - Create ProvenanceRecord, sign, store in provenance DB
   - Fail-open: if provenance capture fails, log warning but don't block the tool call

   - Implement Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON format (per github.com/cursor/agent-trace spec)
   - `fn to_agent_trace(record: &ProvenanceRecord) -> Value` — convert to spec JSON
   - `fn export_agent_trace(records: Vec<ProvenanceRecord>) -> String` — full trace file

9. **Create `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow blame <file>` — line-by-line attribution
   - Output format: `<line_num> | <contributor> | <model_id> | <timestamp> | <code>`
   - Color-coded: human=green, ai=yellow, mixed=cyan, unknown=gray
   - Flag: `--json` for machine-readable output
   - Flag: `--session <id>` to filter by session

    - Add `Blame` variant to Commands enum
    - Route to blame_cmd handler

    - Unit: content_hash (known vectors), attestation (sign/verify roundtrip), provenance (CRUD)
    - Integration: mock PreToolUse/PostToolUse JSON → verify provenance record created
    - CLI: `codeflow blame` on test fixture files

# Phase 1: Foundation — Proto Schema + Provenance Core

## Overview

Establish event schema (protobuf), content hashing (blake3), signed attestation (Ed25519), and the `codeflow blame` CLI command. This phase creates the data foundation all other pillars depend on.

## Requirements

- Functional: capture model_id, prompt hash, code hash, file paths, contributor type at point-of-generation via PreToolUse/PostToolUse hooks; sign provenance records with Ed25519; export Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON; `codeflow blame` command shows line-by-line AI attribution
- Non-functional: <5ms hook latency (fail-open); provenance DB <50MB for 90 days typical usage; zero network dependency for local operation

## Architecture

**Critical constraint:** Only PreToolUse hooks exist. PostToolUse does NOT exist in any agent's hook protocol. Each hook invocation is a separate OS process — no shared in-memory state. Hook JSON payload contains only `tool_name` + `tool_input.command` — no `model_id`.

```
PreToolUse hook (tool N) → snapshot working tree state (file hashes)
    ↓ (agent executes tool, modifies files)
PreToolUse hook (tool N+1) → diff working tree vs snapshot → detect changes from tool N
    ↓
ProvenanceRecord { model_id: "unknown"/enriched, code_hash, file_path, lines, attestation_sig }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db, WAL mode) ← single DB, no split-brain
    ↓
Protobuf event → EVENT_TYPE_PROVENANCE → queued for export
```

**Provenance capture strategy:** Since PostToolUse doesn't exist, use "diff-on-next-PreToolUse" pattern:
1. Each PreToolUse: read last snapshot from DB, diff current working tree against it, record changes as provenance from previous tool call
2. Store new snapshot for next comparison
3. Fallback: `codeflow blame --retroactive` scans git history for attribution after the fact

**model_id enrichment:** Hook JSON has no model_id. Strategies:
1. Parse from ccusage session data (retroactive, but accurate)
2. Infer from agent config files (`.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/config.json`)
3. Accept "unknown" as valid — enrich later when data available

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/mod.rs` — export new provenance module
- Modify: `src/core/mod.rs` — export provenance module

- Create: `src/core/provenance.rs` — ProvenanceRecord struct, signing, storage
- Create: `src/core/attestation.rs` — Ed25519 key management, sign/verify
- Create: `src/core/content_hash.rs` — blake3 hashing for code content
- Create: `src/core/agent_trace.rs` — Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export format
- Create: `src/cmds/blame_cmd.rs` — `codeflow blame` command implementation

   - `fn hash_file(path: &Path) -> Result<String>` — hash file contents
   - `fn hash_diff(old: &str, new: &str) -> String` — hash the diff

5. **Create `src/core/attestation.rs`**
   - `struct KeyPair` — wraps Ed25519 keypair
   - `fn generate_keypair() -> KeyPair` — auto-generate, store at `dirs::data_dir()/rtk/keys/` (cross-platform via `dirs` crate, already in Cargo.toml)
   - `fn load_or_generate() -> Result<KeyPair>` — lazy init
   - `fn sign(keypair: &KeyPair, data: &[u8]) -> String` — hex-encoded signature

   - Flag: `--json` for machine-readable output
   - Flag: `--session <id>` to filter by session

10. **Wire into main.rs**
    - Add `Blame` variant to Commands enum
    - Route to blame_cmd handler

11. **Tests**
    - Unit: content_hash (known vectors), attestation (sign/verify roundtrip), provenance (CRUD)
    - Integration: mock PreToolUse/PostToolUse JSON → verify provenance record created
    - CLI: `codeflow blame` on test fixture files

## Success Criteria

- [ ] `proto/events.proto` compiles with prost-build, generates Rust types
- [ ] Ed25519 keypair auto-generated on first use, persisted at `~/.local/share/rtk/keys/`
- [ ] ProvenanceRecord created for every PostToolUse file-write event
- [ ] `codeflow blame <file>` shows line-by-line AI attribution with model_id
- [ ] Agent Trace v0.1.0 JSON export passes format validation
- [ ] Hook latency remains <5ms (benchmark test)
- [ ] Existing RTK tests still pass (no regression)
- [ ] 15+ new tests for provenance, attestation, content_hash, blame

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Claude Code doesn't expose model_id in hook JSON | HIGH | Parse from session metadata; fallback to "unknown" with flag |
| prost-build adds Windows build complexity | MEDIUM | Use pre-generated .rs files as fallback; CI builds on Linux |
| Provenance DB grows too large | LOW | 90-day retention (reuse tracking.rs pattern); vacuum on startup |

## Security Considerations

- Ed25519 private key stored with 0600 permissions (Unix) or ACL-restricted (Windows)
- Never log private key material
- Attestation signatures are non-repudiable — document this for users
- Content hashes use blake3 (cryptographic) not xxhash (fast but not cryptographic)

# Phase 2: Cost Attribution Engine

## Overview

Attribute every token to a specific session → PR → feature. Extend existing `tracking.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` with PR linkage, model pricing lookup, and cost-per-PR calculations. Add `codeflow cost` CLI command.

## Requirements

- Functional: link sessions to PRs via git branch metadata; calculate dollar cost per session/PR/feature; model pricing table (updatable); `codeflow cost` command shows cost breakdown by PR/dev/project
- Non-functional: cost calculation adds <1ms per event; pricing table updatable without recompile; backward-compatible with existing tracking.db

## Architecture

```
PostToolUse hook (existing) → token counts (already captured in tracking.rs)
    ↓
+ Extract PR ref from: git branch name, commit message, env vars (GH_PR_NUMBER)
+ Lookup model pricing: model_id → $/1M input tokens, $/1M output tokens
    ↓
CostRecord { session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db with cost_records table)
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_COST → queued for cloud sync
```

**Existing assets to extend:**
- `tracking.rs:TimedExecution` — already tracks input/output tokens per command
- `ccusage.rs` — already parses Claude Code spending from ccusage CLI
- `cc_economics.rs` — already computes cost-per-token, blended/active CPT
- `session_cmd.rs` — already analyzes sessions for RTK adoption

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add cost_records table, PR linkage fields
- Modify: `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs` — integrate per-PR cost rollups
- Modify: `src/analytics/session_cmd.rs` — add cost column to session analysis
- Modify: `src/analytics/mod.rs` — export cost module
- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — extract PR ref in PostToolUse, emit CostEvent
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `cost` subcommand
- Create: `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs` — `codeflow cost` command
- Create: `src/core/pricing.rs` — model pricing table + lookup
- Create: `src/core/pr_linker.rs` — git branch → PR linkage logic
- Create: `data/model-pricing.toml` — default pricing table (updatable)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `data/model-pricing.toml`**
   ```toml
   [models.claude-opus-4]
   input_per_mtok = 15.0
   output_per_mtok = 75.0
   cache_read_per_mtok = 1.5
   cache_write_per_mtok = 18.75

   [models.claude-sonnet-4]
   input_per_mtok = 3.0
   output_per_mtok = 15.0
   # ... etc for GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/pricing.rs`**
   - Load from `data/model-pricing.toml` (bundled) or `~/.config/rtk/model-pricing.toml` (user override)
   - `fn cost_for_tokens(model_id: &str, input: u64, output: u64, cache_read: u64, cache_write: u64) -> f64`
   - Fallback: if model_id unknown, use median pricing + log warning

3. **Create `src/core/pr_linker.rs`**
   - `fn detect_pr_ref() -> Option<String>` — try in order:
     1. Env var `GH_PR_NUMBER` or `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`
     2. Parse git branch name: `feat/PROJ-123-description` → `PROJ-123`
     3. Parse recent commit messages for `(#123)` pattern
     4. `gh pr view --json number` if gh CLI available
   - `fn detect_feature_tag() -> Option<String>` — from branch prefix or git tag

4. **Extend tracking.db schema**
   - New table: `cost_records (id, session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, project_path, developer_id, timestamp)`
   - Migration: add table if not exists (backward-compatible)

5. **Extend `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - In PostToolUse: after existing token tracking, compute cost via pricing.rs
   - Detect PR ref via pr_linker.rs
   - Insert CostRecord into tracking.db
   - Emit EVENT_TYPE_COST protobuf event

6. **Create `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow cost` — summary of costs for current project
   - `codeflow cost --by pr` — cost breakdown by PR
   - `codeflow cost --by dev` — cost breakdown by developer
   - `codeflow cost --by model` — cost breakdown by model
   - `codeflow cost --by day` — daily cost trend
   - `codeflow cost --pr 1234` — specific PR cost detail
   - `codeflow cost --json` — machine-readable output
   - Reuse display_helpers.rs formatting patterns

7. **Extend `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs`**
   - Add `fn cost_per_pr(tracker: &Tracker, pr_ref: &str) -> PeriodEconomics`
   - Add PR column to economics table output

8. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Cost` variant to Commands enum

9. **Tests**
   - Unit: pricing lookup (known model → expected cost), pr_linker (branch patterns)
   - Integration: mock PostToolUse → verify CostRecord in DB with correct cost_usd
   - CLI: `codeflow cost --by pr` with fixture data
   - 12+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Model pricing table covers Claude (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku), GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
- [ ] PR linkage detects PR ref from >=2 of the 4 detection methods
- [ ] `codeflow cost` shows total cost for current project with breakdown
- [ ] `codeflow cost --by pr` shows per-PR cost ranking
- [ ] Cost records stored in tracking.db, backward-compatible migration
- [ ] Existing `rtk economics` command still works (no regression)
- [ ] 12+ new tests for pricing, pr_linker, cost_cmd

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Model pricing changes frequently | LOW | TOML file updatable; CLI flag `--update-pricing` fetches latest |
| PR detection fails in detached HEAD CI | MEDIUM | Fallback to "unknown" PR; CI env vars as primary source |
| tracking.db migration breaks existing data | MEDIUM | ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN; test migration path |

# Phase 2: Cost Attribution Engine

## Overview

Attribute every token to a specific session → PR → feature. Extend existing `tracking.rs` + `cc_economics.rs` with PR linkage, model pricing lookup, and cost-per-PR calculations. Add `codeflow cost` CLI command.

## Requirements

- Functional: link sessions to PRs via git branch metadata; calculate dollar cost per session/PR/feature; model pricing table (updatable); `codeflow cost` command shows cost breakdown by PR/dev/project
- Non-functional: cost calculation adds <1ms per event; pricing table updatable without recompile; backward-compatible with existing tracking.db

## Architecture

**Critical constraint:** No PostToolUse hook exists. Cost data comes from ccusage (actual API billing), not hook-captured tokens.

```
ccusage CLI (actual Anthropic billing) → parsed by ccusage.rs
    ↓
+ `codeflow cost sync` → import ccusage sessions into tracking.db cost_records
+ Extract PR ref from: git branch name, commit message, env vars (GH_PR_NUMBER)
+ Match session timestamps to PR activity windows
    ↓
CostRecord { session_id, model_id, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, source: "ccusage" }
    ↓
SQLite (extend tracking.db with cost_records table)
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_COST → queued for export
```

**Existing assets to extend:**
- `ccusage.rs` — **authoritative cost source** — parses actual Anthropic API billing data
- `cc_economics.rs` — computes cost-per-token from ccusage (billing truth)
- `session_cmd.rs` — session analysis for adoption metrics

**IMPORTANT — dual cost system clarification (Finding #4, #8):**
- `tracking.rs` tracks RTK **compression** tokens (input string size vs filtered output size), NOT LLM API tokens. Do NOT use tracking.rs token counts for cost calculation.
- `ccusage` provides actual API billing data — this is the authoritative cost source.
- New `CostRecord` table provides **attribution metadata** (which PR/feature/dev consumed cost), NOT billing truth. Attribution links ccusage billing data to PRs, not a parallel cost system.

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add cost_records table, PR linkage fields
- Modify: `src/analytics/cc_economics.rs` — integrate per-PR cost rollups
- Modify: `src/analytics/session_cmd.rs` — add cost column to session analysis
- Modify: `src/analytics/mod.rs` — export cost module
- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — extract PR ref in PreToolUse (no PostToolUse exists), store as session metadata
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `cost` subcommand
- Create: `src/analytics/cost_cmd.rs` — `codeflow cost` command
- Create: `src/core/pricing.rs` — model pricing table + lookup
- Create: `src/core/pr_linker.rs` — git branch → PR linkage logic
- Create: `data/model-pricing.toml` — default pricing table (updatable)

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create `data/model-pricing.toml`**
   ```toml
   [models.claude-opus-4]
   input_per_mtok = 15.0
   output_per_mtok = 75.0
   cache_read_per_mtok = 1.5
   cache_write_per_mtok = 18.75

   [models.claude-sonnet-4]
   input_per_mtok = 3.0
   output_per_mtok = 15.0
   # ... etc for GPT-4o, Gemini, Codex
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/pricing.rs`**
   - Load from `data/model-pricing.toml` (bundled) or `~/.config/rtk/model-pricing.toml` (user override)
   - `fn cost_for_tokens(model_id: &str, input: u64, output: u64, cache_read: u64, cache_write: u64) -> f64`
   - Fallback: if model_id unknown, use median pricing + log warning

3. **Create `src/core/pr_linker.rs`**
   - `fn detect_pr_ref() -> Option<String>` — try in order:
     1. Env var `GH_PR_NUMBER` or `GITHUB_PR_NUMBER`
     2. Parse git branch name: `feat/PROJ-123-description` → `PROJ-123`
     3. Parse recent commit messages for `(#123)` pattern
     4. `gh pr view --json number` if gh CLI available
   - `fn detect_feature_tag() -> Option<String>` — from branch prefix or git tag

4. **Extend tracking.db schema**
   - New table: `cost_records (id, session_id, model_id, input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_read_tokens, cache_write_tokens, cost_usd, pr_ref, feature_tag, project_path, developer_id, timestamp)`
   - Migration: add table if not exists (backward-compatible)

   - `codeflow cost --by dev` — cost breakdown by developer
   - `codeflow cost --by model` — cost breakdown by model
   - `codeflow cost --by day` — daily cost trend
   - `codeflow cost --pr 1234` — specific PR cost detail
   - `codeflow cost --json` — machine-readable output
   - Reuse display_helpers.rs formatting patterns

   - Add `fn cost_per_pr(tracker: &Tracker, pr_ref: &str) -> PeriodEconomics`
   - Add PR column to economics table output

# Phase 3: Budget Governance + Policy Engine

## Overview

Real-time budget enforcement in PreToolUse hooks. Policy engine evaluates per-dev, per-project, per-team spending limits and can warn, downgrade model, or block tool calls that exceed budget.

## Requirements

- Functional: TOML-based policy definitions (per-dev, per-project, per-team limits); PreToolUse budget check (warn/downgrade/block); alert webhooks on threshold breach; `codeflow budget` CLI for status/policy management
- Non-functional: policy evaluation <2ms; fail-open if policy engine errors; policies hot-reloadable without restart

## Architecture

```
PreToolUse hook → read accumulated cost for {dev, project, team} from tracking.db
    ↓
PolicyEngine.evaluate(context) → Verdict { Allow | Warn(msg) | Downgrade(to_model) | Block(reason) }
    ↓
If Block → return error JSON to agent (tool call rejected)
If Downgrade → rewrite model_id in hook response
If Warn → log warning, allow tool call
    ↓
GovernanceEvent { policy_id, action, reason, budget_remaining, developer_id }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_GOVERNANCE → queued for cloud sync
```

## Related Code Files

- Modify: `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs` — add budget check in PreToolUse before command rewrite
- Modify: `src/core/tracking.rs` — add query for accumulated cost by dev/project/team/period
- Modify: `src/main.rs` — add `budget` subcommand
- Create: `src/core/budget_policy.rs` — policy engine: load, evaluate, verdicts
- Create: `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs` — `codeflow budget` CLI
- Create: `data/budget-policy-example.toml` — example policy file

## Implementation Steps

1. **Define policy schema in `data/budget-policy-example.toml`**
   ```toml
   [global]
   period = "monthly"
   warn_at_pct = 75
   block_at_pct = 100

   [[limits]]
   scope = "developer"
   id = "*"
   max_usd = 500.0
   action_on_exceed = "warn"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "project"
   id = "frontend-app"
   max_usd = 2000.0
   action_on_exceed = "downgrade"
   downgrade_to = "claude-haiku-4"

   [[limits]]
   scope = "team"
   id = "platform"
   max_usd = 10000.0
   action_on_exceed = "block"
   ```

2. **Create `src/core/budget_policy.rs`**
   - `struct PolicyConfig` — deserialized from TOML
   - `struct PolicyEngine` — loads config, caches accumulated costs
   - `enum Verdict { Allow, Warn(String), Downgrade(String), Block(String) }`
   - `fn evaluate(&self, dev_id: &str, project: &str, team: &str) -> Verdict`
   - Load policy from: project `.codeflow/budget.toml` → user `~/.config/rtk/budget.toml` → bundled default
   - Accumulated cost query: sum cost_records WHERE scope AND period

3. **Extend PreToolUse in `src/hooks/hook_cmd.rs`**
   - Before command rewrite: run PolicyEngine.evaluate()
   - If Block: return JSON error `{"error": "budget_exceeded", ...}`
   - If Downgrade: modify model_id in response
   - If Warn: write warning to stderr, continue
   - Fail-open on any error

4. **Extend `src/core/tracking.rs`**
   - `fn accumulated_cost(&self, scope: Scope, id: &str, period: Period) -> f64`
   - Index on (scope, period_start) for performance

5. **Create `src/cmds/budget_cmd.rs`**
   - `codeflow budget status` — current spend vs limits for all scopes
   - `codeflow budget set --scope dev --id alice --max 500` — quick policy update
   - `codeflow budget history` — spending trend with budget overlay
   - `codeflow budget alert --webhook <url>` — configure alert endpoint

6. **Alert system**
   - On threshold breach: POST to webhook URL with JSON payload
   - Use `ureq` (already in deps) for HTTP POST
   - Fire-and-forget: don't block hook on webhook delivery

7. **Wire into main.rs** — add `Budget` variant to Commands enum

8. **Tests**
   - Unit: policy parsing (valid/invalid TOML), verdict evaluation (under/warn/over)
   - Integration: mock PreToolUse with accumulated cost → verify block/downgrade/warn
   - CLI: `codeflow budget status` with fixture policies
   - 10+ new tests

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Policy TOML parsed correctly with per-dev, per-project, per-team limits
- [ ] PreToolUse blocks tool call when budget exceeded (block action)
- [ ] PreToolUse downgrades model when budget tight (downgrade action)
- [ ] `codeflow budget status` shows current spend vs limits
- [ ] Webhook alerts fire on threshold breach
- [ ] Fail-open: policy engine error → tool call proceeds with warning
- [ ] 10+ new tests

## Risk Assessment

| Risk | Severity | Mitigation |
|------|----------|------------|
| Blocking tool calls frustrates developers | HIGH | Default to warn-only; block requires explicit opt-in |
| Model downgrade breaks agentic sessions | MEDIUM | Only downgrade for new sessions, not mid-session |
| Cost accumulation query slow with large DB | LOW | Index on (scope, period_start) |

Real-time budget enforcement in PreToolUse hooks. Policy engine evaluates per-dev, per-project, per-team spending limits and can warn, downgrade model, or block tool calls that exceed budget.

- Non-functional: policy evaluation <2ms; fail-open if policy engine errors; policies hot-reloadable without restart

**Critical constraints (from red-team):**

    ↓
GovernanceEvent { policy_id, action, reason, budget_remaining, developer_id }
    ↓
Protobuf EVENT_TYPE_GOVERNANCE → queued for export
